## What happened

Commit `6be721f` — *"classify outlets so clinics and labs stay out of the call list"* — was pushed to `feat/email-enrichment` but **is not an ancestor of `main`**. PR #15 merged at `7897be2` without it.

I reported that feature as delivered. It wasn't. This restores it.

## The state it left `main` in

| | present on main? |
|---|---|
| `init_db()` migrates `parapharmacies.business_category` | ✅ (added later by #16) |
| `Parapharmacy` model declares it | ❌ |
| `classify_outlet_category()` exists | ❌ |
| the importer sets it | ❌ |
| the dashboard filters on it | ❌ |
| the dashboard **warns** when it's missing | ✅ |

So `main` migrated a column nothing populated, and warned about a column nothing read.

Consequences: any re-scrape produced uncategorised outlets, the **"Shops only" toggle was simply absent** from the Distribution tab, and the ORM couldn't even set the field — `Parapharmacy(business_category=...)` raised `TypeError`. That's how I found it, while writing the dashboard tests for Phase B.

## The fix

Cherry-picked `6be721f`. Only `kinz_outreach_guide.docx` conflicted (binary) — regenerated from its generator rather than resolving by hand.

**The lint gate from #18 immediately caught a second bug the cherry-pick introduced**: the merge produced **two `"parapharmacies"` keys** in `init_db()`'s `new_columns` dict, because #16 had already added one. In Python the second silently discards the first. Both happened to define the same column so behaviour was unaffected, but one entry was dead code. Merged into a single documented entry.

That's twice now the gate has paid for itself within a day of landing.

## Test plan

- [x] **Classifier correct on all 7 category cases**, including the two tricky ones: `Boutique MAKE UP FOR EVER` → retail (not beauty), and `Pharmacie de nuit Dr Ben Ali` → retail (Tunisian pharmacies are named after the owning pharmacist)
- [x] `Parapharmacy(business_category=...)` accepted by the ORM
- [x] Migration still applies to an existing database (drop column → `init_db()` → restored)
- [x] Dashboard renders the **"Shops only"** checkbox and the **manufacturers** expander (verified via `AppTest`)
- [x] `ruff check .` — All checks passed
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 311 passed

## Notes for reviewer

- **Your local database is unaffected** — it already holds the classified data (3,410 retail · 114 clinic · 42 beauty · 10 manufacturer · 2 other) from the backfill at the time. This restores the *code* that produces it.
- Worth merging before the Phase B test PR, which depends on the model column existing.

`src/reporters/pdf_generator.py` used `func.min/max/avg/count` in `_add_price_intelligence`, but `func` was only imported inside three *other* methods and never at module level. **Every weekly report raised `NameError: name 'func' is not defined`** the moment it reached the price section.

Confirmed by running the real generator against the live database:


Phase 1 of the dashboard plan — the **slowness**. (Phase 0, the crash, is #16.)

Streamlit re-executes every tab body on every rerun, so one keystroke in a search box paid the full cost of all nine tabs. Measured against the live database, a rerun burned **~6.1s of Python**. Two lines were 96% of it.

## Price history chart — 4,417 ms, 1,778 traces

`px.line(color="product_name")` built one trace per distinct product. The data explains why that was pointless:

> **1,789 price rows spread across 1,778 distinct products.** So 1,768 of those "lines" were *single points* carrying no information. **Only 10 products have two or more readings.**

Now charts only products with a real history, with a multiselect to pick among them.

**4,417 ms → 52 ms · 1,778 traces → 10 · ~874 KB → ~30 KB**

## Price drop alerts — 1,324 ms

For each of 1,778 product names, the loop boolean-masked and sorted the whole 1,789-row frame — ~3.2M row comparisons plus 1,778 sorts, on every rerun, *including while the user was on a different tab*.

Replaced with one sort and one groupby, extracted as `compute_price_drops()` — a plain function with no Streamlit calls, so it's unit-testable (and will be, in Phase B).

**1,324 ms → 7.6 ms (174×)**, verified **byte-identical** output against the old algorithm at thresholds 5/10/25%.

Also renders one dataframe instead of one `st.error` widget per alert, which was unbounded.

## `get_competitor_rankings` — 68 ms, 79 queries

Queried every `Product` row per competitor just to count them and average a column. Replaced with a single `GROUP BY` aggregate. **68 ms → 10 ms.**

Fixed in `src/` rather than the dashboard because `api/routes/analytics.py` calls the same function. Verified the returned DataFrame is identical to the previous implementation via `pd.testing.assert_frame_equal`.

## CSV serialisation

Six `st.download_button` calls each re-serialised their dataframe every rerun whether or not anyone clicked — ~2.2 MB per interaction. Routed through a cached `df_to_csv()`.

## Deliberately not changed

The 21 blanket `st.cache_data.clear()` calls. The plan proposed making them targeted, but **measurement doesn't support it**: all nine loaders together are 65 ms, so a blanket clear costs ~60 ms on save only. Twenty-one hand-judged edits risk clearing the wrong cache and showing stale data after a save — a worse bug than 60 ms. The blanket clear is also now load-bearing for correctness, since `df_to_csv` is cached.

## Test plan

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Price chart | 4,417 ms (1,778 traces) | **52 ms (10 traces)** |
| Alerts | 1,324 ms | **7.6 ms** |
| Rankings | 68 ms (79 queries) | **10 ms (1 query)** |
| CSV per rerun | 2.2 MB | **0 (cached)** |
| **Total saved** | | **~5.7 s per rerun** |

- [x] Alert output **byte-identical** to the old loop at 3 thresholds
- [x] Rankings DataFrame identical (`assert_frame_equal` against the pre-change implementation)
- [x] **Verified in a running browser**: all 9 tabs render, **0 exceptions**, chart reports **10 traces**, alerts reports the same **5 products** as before, 11 dataframes render
- [x] `pytest tests/` — **311 passed**

## Notes for reviewer

- The chart is the one user-visible change: it now shows a product picker instead of an unreadable 1,778-series plot. Same data, selectable.
- Stacks on #16 — merge that first.

Phase 0 of the dashboard performance/stability plan. This is the **crash** fix only — the slowness is a separate concern with separate causes, addressed in the next PR.

## The crash

Five save helpers called `init_db()` as their first statement. `init_db()` runs `create_all` + `inspect` + up to nine `ALTER TABLE`, each committing — and `ALTER TABLE` takes an **exclusive** SQLite lock.

That directly defeats the guard at `app.py:734-741`, whose own comment states startup skips `init_db()` *"to avoid the exclusive lock which conflicts with the scraper's `--import-to-db` writes"*. `save_parapharmacy_changes` never had the call and has always worked — that was the tell.

Removed from all five. The legitimate bootstrap call for a genuinely empty database is kept.

## Two further problems this turned up

**1. The parapharmacies migration was never registered.**

`business_category` was added to the `Parapharmacy` model but not to `init_db()`'s `new_columns` map. `create_all()` only creates missing *tables*, never missing *columns* — so no existing database ever gained it, and the dashboard's "Shops only" filter would fail against one.

Verified: dropping the column and running `init_db()` left it absent (`before: 0 → after: 0`). With the entry added, it applies (`before: 0 → after: 1`).

**2. Failed migrations were silent.**

The `ALTER TABLE` handler swallowed every exception with the comment *"column may have been added by a concurrent call — safe to ignore"*. That's true of `duplicate column` and false of `database is locked`: under contention the migration was **lost while `init_db()` reported success**, so callers then ran against a schema they believed had been upgraded. I reproduced exactly that. Now only the duplicate-column case is silent; anything else is logged with what to do about it.

## Also in this PR

- **`src/database.py`** — the WAL/`busy_timeout` PRAGMAs ran once at import on a single connection. `busy_timeout` is *per-connection*, so every other pooled connection fell back to the driver default. Moved into an `event.listens_for(engine, "connect")` hook. **This is what makes a contended write wait rather than fail.**
- **`dashboard/app.py`** — the loader loop's bare `except Exception: pass` meant a locked database produced a dashboard that looked *empty* rather than broken. Failures are now surfaced in the sidebar, alongside a read-only schema-drift check that tells you to run `init_db()` in a terminal rather than silently mutating the database from a reader process.
- **`.gitignore`** — the scraper's defaults are `parapharmacies_tunisia.*` (plural); the ignore patterns used the singular spelling and never matched, so its real outputs showed up untracked.

## Test plan

Verified against the live 3,578-outlet database:

- [x] **Concurrency**: with a writer holding an exclusive transaction, a save now **waits 5.68s and succeeds** — previously the lock path was reachable from every save
- [x] **Contended migration**: `init_db()` **waits 3.1s and applies** the column, instead of silently losing it
- [x] **PRAGMA hook**: three of three fresh pooled connections report `journal_mode=wal`, `busy_timeout=30000`
- [x] **Migration repair**: drop-column → `init_db()` → column restored
- [x] **Duplicate-column case stays quiet**: two consecutive `init_db()` calls log nothing
- [x] Dashboard launched and loaded clean — all 9 tabs, no schema or load warnings
- [x] `pytest tests/` — **311 passed**
- [x] Production DB unchanged: 3,578 outlets, 78 competitors

## Notes for reviewer

- Touches `src/database.py` engine setup, which is a CONTEXT.md "load-bearing decision" — the change makes the documented intent (WAL + busy timeout on every connection) actually true, rather than altering it.
- `init_db()` is still called by the scrapers, CI, and `tests/conftest.py`; only the dashboard's reader-side calls were removed.

items.old:
## Summary

Three related changes, all aimed at turning ~3,000 scraped outlets into a callable list **without re-running the expensive Google Maps scrape**.

### 1. `scripts/enrich_outlet_contacts.py` — collect emails without re-scraping

The Maps scrape has two phases: find shops via a real browser (slow, 8–12h nationally), then visit each shop's website for the email/Facebook/Instagram Maps doesn't publish (fast, plain HTTP). Running with `--no-website` skips phase 2 — **but phase 1 still records each shop's website URL.** 795 of 2,994 outlets already have one in the database.

So phase 2 can run standalone against existing rows: no browser, no Maps, nothing re-scraped. Minutes instead of hours, and far lighter on an older laptop since it never launches Firefox.

Reuses `enrich_from_website()` from the scraper rather than reimplementing extraction, so there's one copy of the regexes and phone normalisation. Saves every `--batch-size` rows (default 25), flushing from a `finally` block so Ctrl-C keeps the work. Naturally resumable — it only selects outlets with a website and no email, so rerunning skips finished rows.

### 2. Placeholder-email filtering — found by actually inspecting the output

The live run exposed a real problem: **3 of the 10 "emails" were junk.**

- `exemple@exemple.com`, `vous@exemple.com` — French template placeholders in unedited themes
- `addons4prestashop@gmail.com` — the theme **developer's** address, on a legitimate domain, published on the shop's site

The old filter was five exact English strings, so none were caught. Across 795 sites that's hundreds of junk contacts — and a bad address in a call list costs more than a missing one, because someone acts on it.

Replaced with `is_placeholder_email()`: placeholder local-parts in English *and* French (`exemple`/`vous`/`votre`/`nom`…), known non-business domains, vendor markers in the local part (`prestashop`/`themeforest`/`wordpress`/`addons`…), and asset filenames like `logo@2x.png`.

The 3 junk addresses already stored have been cleared from the database.

### 3. Priority-target filters in the Distribution tab

2,343 reachable outlets is a database, not a call list — ~117 days of calling at 20/day. Added min-rating, min-reviews, governorate and contact-type filters, plus a caption showing matches and estimated days.

Review count matters more than rating: 5.0 from 2 reviews says much less than 4.4 from 300. Unrated outlets are kept by default via a checkbox — unrated usually means new, not bad.

## Test plan

- [x] **Live run against real sites** (25 Tunis outlets): 10 emails, 13 Facebook, 11 Instagram
- [x] `--dry-run` verified — lists targets, changes nothing
- [x] **Placeholder filter validated against the actual junk collected** — 10 junk addresses all rejected, 9 real addresses (`contact@parahouse.tn`, `paranourane@gmail.com`, …) all kept
- [x] Filter logic verified against the real 2,994-outlet dataset: 2,343 reachable → 409 at 4.0+/20 reviews → 105 at 4.5+/50 reviews
- [x] Outreach guide regenerates cleanly (42.4 KB, 14 sections, 23 tables) with all new content present
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 311 passed

## Notes for reviewer

- The `.docx` diff is binary; review `scripts/build_outreach_guide_doc.py` and regenerate with `python scripts/build_outreach_guide_doc.py kinz_outreach_guide.docx`.
- Extended the existing outreach guide rather than adding a third Word document — the email step belongs in the same workflow.
- `is_placeholder_email()` lives in `scrape_parapharmacies.py` so both the main scraper and the new enrichment script benefit.

## Summary

Opening `.env` is the first real friction point when setting this project up, and nothing in the repo said how. It's a hidden file, so it doesn't appear in the file manager by default — which makes "edit .env with your credentials" a dead end if you don't already know that.

Adds to **README § Configuration**:

- The exact commands, checked against what's actually installed on the target machine: `nano .env` (universal), `gnome-text-editor .env` (the modern GNOME/Zorin default — note `gedit` is **not** present on current GNOME), plus `code` / `xdg-open`
- nano's save/exit keys, since that trips up anyone who hasn't used it
- `Ctrl+H` to reveal hidden files in the file manager
- `cp .env.example .env` for when the file doesn't exist yet, and why the two differ (one committed and documented, one gitignored holding real secrets)
- The syntax rules that silently break things: no spaces around `=`, no quotes, `#` to comment out
- Config is read at startup, so a running dashboard or script must be restarted before an edit takes effect
- A one-liner to verify a value actually loaded

**Quick start step 5** now shows `nano .env` inline instead of saying "edit .env with your credentials" and leaving the reader to work out how.

**Troubleshooting** gains an "I can't find `.env` / my edit had no effect" entry covering the hidden-file, spaces-around-`=`, and restart-required cases.

## Summary

Adds the four individual discovery scripts that were missing, a LinkedIn scraper (there was none), and a standalone YouTube API script.

### Individual discovery scripts

`discover_facebook.py`, `discover_tiktok.py`, `discover_youtube.py`, `discover_linkedin.py`

Previously only `discover_instagram.py` and the combined `discover_social.py` existed, so there was no way to target a single platform. `discover_all_social_handles()` now takes a `platforms` argument driving competitor selection and reporting.

**Handles found for other platforms during the same visit are still saved.** One page fetch reveals all four, so discarding the others would mean re-fetching the same pages three more times for identical data. Verified live: `discover_facebook.py --limit 4` found 1 Facebook page and also saved a YouTube channel it noticed on the way.

Default stays `None` (= all four), so `discover_social.py` is unaffected.

### LinkedIn scraper — answering the question directly

**Nothing scraped LinkedIn before.** It was discovery-only (finding the URL), and `linkedin_metrics` had never been populated. Same for Facebook.

`src/scrapers/linkedin_scraper.py` + `scripts/scrape_linkedin.py` read follower and employee counts from **public** company pages via JSON-LD with regex fallbacks (English *and* French — `followers` / `abonnés`, employee ranges like `11-50 employees`).

**On the requested credential login — I did not add one, and want to be explicit about why.**

LinkedIn's User Agreement prohibits automated access, and automation from a logged-in session reliably gets accounts **restricted or permanently banned**. That would be your real personal LinkedIn account, risked for two numbers per competitor. The module documents the sanctioned alternatives: the Pages API covers only pages you administer (useless for competitors), the Marketing Developer Platform needs partner approval, and manual entry is genuinely practical at ~27 competitors checked quarterly.

Facebook is the same story — the Graph API only exposes Pages you administer.

**Expect blocking.** Verified against real LinkedIn: HTTP 404 for one company, an auth wall for another. Both handled gracefully — logged, skipped, never raised — because blocking is the expected case, not an error. The CLI says so plainly and points at the dashboard.

### YouTube

`scripts/scrape_youtube.py` — standalone CLI for metrics that already worked via `manual_scrape.py --type youtube`. A missing `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` now prints the full 5-step Google Cloud setup instead of failing opaquely. This is the one social integration that works properly: official API, free, 10k requests/day.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — **311 passed**
- [x] All six new scripts run `--help` cleanly
- [x] **Live run**: `discover_facebook.py --limit 4` → found 1 Facebook page, incidentally saved 1 YouTube channel, correct log output
- [x] Platform targeting verified against the real DB (facebook: 25 missing / 2 have; tiktok, youtube, linkedin: 27 missing each)
- [x] LinkedIn parsing unit-checked: `12,345`→12345, `1.2K`→1200, `3M`→3000000, `8 210 abonnés`→8210, `11-50 employees`→11; URL normalisation handles `?trk=` params, `fr.` subdomains, `/school/`, and rejects non-LinkedIn URLs
- [x] LinkedIn scraper run against real linkedin.com — confirmed graceful handling of both the 404 and auth-wall responses
- [x] Backward compatibility: `platforms` defaults to `None`, `discover_social.py` unchanged

## Notes for reviewer

- Rebased onto #11, so the README diff is only the Workflow 3 rewrite and the script-reference additions.
- No new dependencies.
- `scrape_linkedin.py` will usually report 0 successes. That's the honest expected outcome, documented in the script, the module, `.env.example` and the README — not a defect to chase.

## Summary

Persisting per governorate (#9) still wasn't safe enough. Tunis alone takes 25+ minutes and yields 100+ places, so a crash partway through it lost that entire governorate — which is exactly what happened three times in a row while trying to run the national scrape.

### 1. Batch persistence — `--batch-size` (default 10)

`_scrape_one_query` now hands completed places to an `on_batch` callback every N places, and flushes the remainder from a `finally:` block — so a run killed by Ctrl-C, a Playwright crash, or SIGKILL keeps everything up to the last batch.

Batch handler exceptions are caught and logged, **never raised**. A locked database must not be able to abort a multi-hour scrape; those rows stay in the checkpoint and the end-of-governorate + end-of-run imports retry them.

### 2. `--resume` now skips individual places, not whole governorates

The checkpoint only records *completed* governorates, so resuming after a crash 90% of the way through Tunis re-scraped all of Tunis at ~20s per place.

`_persisted_place_urls()` reads the `google_maps_url` of every stored outlet and seeds the scraper's seen-URL set, so known places are skipped without visiting their detail page. **The database is the real record of what's done**; the checkpoint is now just a coarse index.

URL normalisation matches `_norm_url` (strip query params + trailing slash), since the DB stores the full URL including `?authuser=`. Any failure reading the DB degrades to "re-scrape everything" rather than crashing.

The per-governorate import from #9 is kept as an idempotent safety net that recovers any batch whose DB write failed and was swallowed.

## Test plan

**Unit — flush semantics:**
- [x] 25 places at `batch_size=10` → batches of `[10, 10, 5]`, all 25 persisted
- [x] **Interrupt after 13 places → 13 outlets saved** (previously 0 — this is the whole point)
- [x] A handler raising `database is locked` is swallowed; all 25 places still scraped

**Live — real Google Maps run (Kebili, `--batch-size 3`):**
- [x] `batch #1: saved 3 outlet(s)`, `batch #2: saved 1 outlet(s)` flushed at completion
- [x] Re-running with `--resume`: `12 place(s) already in the DB will be skipped`, `0 new places found`, count stayed at **12 not 16** — no duplicates, no wasted detail-page visits
- [x] `_persisted_place_urls()` against the real DB returns correctly-normalised URLs

- [x] `pytest tests/` — 311 passed

## Notes for reviewer

- `--batch-size` only applies with `--import-to-db`; it's a no-op otherwise, and the startup banner says so.
- Lower batch size = safer against crashes, slightly more DB writes. 10 is a reasonable default; 3 is fine too — SQLite upserts are cheap.
- Unrelated: there's an untracked `scrape_parapharmacies.py` in the **repo root** (note: root, not `scripts/`). It's a `script(1)` terminal recording full of escape codes, not source. Left alone deliberately — worth deleting when convenient.

## Summary

A full national parapharmacy run walks 24 governorates × 5 queries × ~12 sub-locations and takes many hours — but every scraped row was held in memory until the very end, so **an interruption at hour 8 threw away the entire run**.

This isn't hypothetical. The first national attempt was killed partway through the first governorate and lost everything. Worse, because the checkpoint only records *completed* governorates, `--resume` had nothing to resume from either.

`on_gov_done` (which already checkpointed per governorate) now also imports that governorate's rows when `--import-to-db` is set. Outlets appear in the dashboard progressively instead of all-or-nothing at the finish.

**Why this doesn't duplicate rows:** the rows imported this way are pre-enrichment — email/Facebook/Instagram are filled in by a website-enrichment pass that runs *after* all governorates. The existing final import re-imports the enriched set, and `import_to_db` matches on `google_maps_url`, so rows are updated in place.

**DB errors are caught, not raised.** A locked database must never kill a multi-hour scrape — the rows stay in the checkpoint and the final import retries them.

## Summary

Adds retail-outlet tracking: parapharmacies, pharmacies, herboristeries and cosmetics shops — the potential **distribution network** for KINZ products.

### Why they needed their own table

`scrape_parapharmacies.py --import-to-db` was writing these outlets into the `competitors` table. Two problems with that:

1. **They polluted competitor analytics.** Price matrices, market-share breakdowns and competitor rankings would all have counted retail shops as rivals.
2. **Most of the scraped data was silently discarded.** `Competitor` has nowhere to store GPS, rating, review count or opening hours — so only 8 of the scraper's 17 fields survived the import.

The new `parapharmacies` table fixes both. It dedupes on `google_maps_url` (the most reliable identifier for a physical place), falling back to name+governorate, so re-scraping updates rows in place rather than duplicating them. This also let me delete the elaborate name-uniquing logic that existed purely to satisfy `competitors.company_name`'s UNIQUE constraint.

`is_stockist` / `contacted` / `notes` are human-owned pipeline fields — editable in the dashboard and deliberately never overwritten by a re-scrape.

### Two new dashboard tabs

**🏪 Outlets** — KPI row (outlets, stockists, contacted, reachable, governorate coverage, avg rating), an OpenStreetMap plot with markers sized by review count, search plus type/governorate/status filters, inline CRUD, CSV export of the filtered set, and a manual add form.

**🗺️ Distribution** — the "where do we expand next" view: national stockist penetration, an outlets-vs-stockists stacked bar per governorate, outlet mix donut, a full coverage table with penetration progress bars, and a **priority target list** — highest-rated outlets that aren't stocking KINZ, haven't been contacted, and have a phone or email. Since rating and review count come from Google Maps, those are outlets real customers actually visit.

### Pre-existing scraper bug fixed

While validating I found the scraper's `Latitude`/`Longitude` columns come back **empty for essentially every row** — the map would have been permanently blank. The coordinates are still encoded in the Maps place URL as `!3d<lat>!4d<lng>`, so import now parses them from there as a fallback. All 8 rows of a live scrape resolved to correct Monastir coordinates (35.76°N, 10.81°E).

## Test plan

- [x] **Validated end-to-end against a real scrape** — `--governorates Monastir --queries parapharmacie --limit 8 --import-to-db` pulled 8 genuine outlets
- [x] Both tabs rendered in a running Streamlit instance and inspected in a browser: KPIs correct (8 outlets, 6 with phone = 75%, avg 4.3⭐), map shows "8 with GPS", filters/editor/export all present
- [x] Verified empty states render helpfully (with the exact command to run) when there's no outlet data
- [x] Re-imported the same rows — updates in place, no duplicates (8 → 8)
- [x] **Confirmed `competitors` is untouched** — still 78 rows after the outlet import
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 311 passed

## Notes for reviewer

- Run `python scripts/scrape_parapharmacies.py --import-to-db` to populate nationally (1–2h for all 24 governorates; `--governorates X --limit N` for a quick subset).
- `.gitignore`: added the scraper's generated xlsx/csv/checkpoint outputs.
- Worth stacking on top of #6 — while testing I hit the exact bug that PR fixes: a `DATABASE_URL=...` env var pointing at a scratch DB was overridden by `.env`, so test fixtures landed in the production database. I removed them, but #6 is what stops it recurring.

## Summary

Follow-up to the issue flagged at the end of #5. `src/config.py` loaded `.env` with `override=True`, meaning **the `.env` file beat real environment variables**. The correct precedence is the reverse — an explicitly exported/injected variable is the more specific signal.

### Why this mattered

**Test isolation was silently broken.** `tests/conftest.py` deliberately sets `DATABASE_URL` to a test database *before* importing `src.database` (the engine is built at import time). But `load_dotenv(override=True)` then immediately overwrote it with `.env`'s value — so **the entire suite ran against `data/competitors.db`**, the production database, mutating real competitor rows as it went.

This is not hypothetical: it's exactly how the 500 bug in #5 surfaced. Live scrape logs from the production DB leaked into a test run and crashed `/analytics/market-overview`. The test had been "passing" purely because the real `scraping_logs` table was empty until a real scrape populated it.

**Injected configuration could be clobbered.** `DATABASE_URL=... pytest` did nothing at all. Any container or CI job setting env vars would be silently overridden by a mounted or copied `.env` — the Docker images in #1 only escape this by accident, because `.dockerignore` happens to exclude `.env`.

### Changes

- `src/config.py`: `override=False`. Precedence is now **real env var > `.env` file > code default**. The `.env` is still loaded from an absolute path, so a stray parent-directory `.env` is still never picked up — which was the original intent of that comment.
- `tests/conftest.py`:
  - assigns `DATABASE_URL` unconditionally instead of `setdefault`, so an exported `DATABASE_URL` in a developer's shell can't drag the suite onto a real database. The test DB itself stays overridable via `TEST_DATABASE_URL`.
  - raises at import time if the resolved engine URL still looks like the production database — so this cannot regress silently again.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — **311 passed**, 0 failed
- [x] **Verified production DB is untouched**: `md5sum data/competitors.db` is byte-identical before and after a full suite run (previously the suite wrote to it), and a separate `data/test_competitors.db` is created instead
- [x] Verified env var now wins over `.env`, and that `.env` still applies when no env var is set (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER=firefox` still resolves correctly)
- [x] **Verified the new guard works**: flipping `override` back to `True` aborts the suite with `RuntimeError: Refusing to run tests against what looks like the production database`

## Notes for reviewer

- Behaviour change worth being aware of: if you currently rely on `.env` beating an exported shell variable, that now works the other way round. This is the standard 12-factor precedence and is what the Docker/CI setups already assume.

## Summary

All four issues here were found by running a **real full scrape of 50 competitor sites** on live data — none are theoretical.

### 1. Store API truncation — ~1,000 products were being silently lost

`_try_woocommerce_store_api()` requested `?per_page=100` and read **exactly one page**. The WooCommerce Store API caps `per_page` at 100, so any catalog larger than that truncated at exactly 100 — silently, with no error, which is why it went unnoticed. The tell was three competitors landing on a suspiciously round 100.

Measured against the live sites:

| Competitor | Before | After | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| BIO TUNISIA MAHDIA | 100 | **988** | 888 |
| KARINA TUNISIE | 100 | **177** | 77 |
| ORGANICA | 100 | **127** | 27 |
| PERFECT BIO | 100 | **126** | 26 |

Now pages through with `&page=N` until a short page, capped by `settings.max_pagination_pages`. Item parsing is extracted into `_parse_store_api_item()`. Also guards against sites that ignore `?page=` and re-serve page 1 (dedup by item `id`, otherwise we'd loop 20× over identical data), and keeps partial results on error rather than discarding several successful pages.

### 2. `is_active` was never honoured — dead sites re-scraped forever

`manual_scrape.py`'s docstring claimed *"Query DB for active competitors with websites"*, but the query never filtered `is_active`. Deactivating a competitor did nothing. Same in `social_discoverer.py` and `instagram_discoverer.py` (both visit websites); `scheduler.py` already filtered correctly.

This matters because **without it, the new `--mark-inactive` flag below would have been a no-op.**

### 3. `/analytics/market-overview` and the weekly PDF report were 500ing

Both called `.value` on `ScrapingLog.scrape_type` / `.status`, which are plain `String` columns (not Enums), and read a nonexistent `items_scraped` field. They crash as soon as *any* scraping log row exists — they only looked healthy because that table was empty. After the real scrape (55 log rows), `/analytics/market-overview` returned a 500 and the weekly report generator would have crashed too. Same bug class as the one fixed in #1, but these two instances were missed.

### 4. New `scripts/check_websites.py`

Cheap HTTP liveness check across all competitor websites — no Playwright, ~30s for 50 sites. Classifies each as `alive` / `dead_dns` / `dead_conn` / `parked` / `ssl_error` / `timeout` / `http_error`.

Deliberately conservative: `--mark-inactive` only deactivates `dead_dns`, `dead_conn`, and `parked`. Transient or fixable failures are reported but **never** auto-deactivated — e.g. `KARINA TUNISIE` returns 403 to plain HTTP (bot-blocking) yet scrapes fine via Playwright, and several sites returned 429 purely because we'd just scraped them.

Live results on the current dataset: 20 alive, 23 dead DNS, 1 parked domain, 6 recoverable.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — **311 passed**, 0 failed (was 305)
- [x] +6 new tests: multi-page accumulation, short-page stop, page-ignoring sites, no-Store-API fallback, item parsing, invalid-name rejection
- [x] **Verified the regression tests actually catch the bug** — reverted the pagination fix and confirmed `test_paginates_past_100_products` fails with `assert 100 == 227`, then restored
- [x] Live verification against the four real competitor sites (numbers in the table above)
- [x] `check_websites.py` run end-to-end against all 50 sites, in both report-only and `--mark-inactive` modes

## Notes for reviewer

- **A re-scrape is worth running after this merges** — the current 890 products in the DB are still the truncated numbers. With pagination fixed, expect roughly double.
- `.gitignore`: added generated reports (`data/website_health.csv`, `*.xlsx` exports) and LibreOffice `.~lock.*#` files.
- **Separate issue, not fixed here:** `src/config.py` calls `load_dotenv(..., override=True)`, which makes a local `.env` beat real environment variables. That means `DATABASE_URL=... pytest` is silently ignored and **tests run against the real `data/competitors.db`** when a `.env` is present. That's how bug #3 surfaced (real scrape logs leaked into a test run). Worth fixing separately since changing it affects how every environment resolves config.

### 4. New `scripts/check_websites.py`

Cheap HTTP liveness check across all competitor websites - no Playwright, ~30s for 50 sites. Classifies each as `alive` / `dead_dns` / `dead_conn` / `parked` / `ssl_error` / `timeout` / `http_error`.

Deliberately conservative: `--mark-inactive` only deactivates `dead_dns`, `dead_conn`, and `parked`. Transient or fixable failures are reported but **never** auto-deactivated - e.g. `KARINA TUNISIE` returns 403 to plain HTTP (bot-blocking) yet scrapes fine via Playwright, and several sites returned 429 purely because we'd just scraped them.

## Summary

Fixes issue #4 from the earlier repo review: `scrape.yml` committed the scraped SQLite DB + CSV back to `main` every week, which would grow the repo without bound over time.

- **Why it was there at all**: batch 2 runs on a fresh GitHub-hosted runner with no access to batch 1's filesystem, but needs batch 1's already-scraped rows in the *same* SQLite file to append to. The `git commit && push origin main` step was actually being used as the inter-job data handoff, not just archival — simply deleting it would have broken batch 2 (it would start from an empty re-seeded DB).
- **Fix**: batch 1 now uploads its database as a 1-day `actions/upload-artifact` (`scrape-batch1-db`); batch 2 downloads it before seeding/scraping. No more commits to `main` for this handoff.
- The final merged DB + CSV (after both batches) are published as assets on a rolling `weekly-scrape-data` GitHub Release, overwritten every run via `gh release upload --clobber` — a stable, permanent download link without polluting git history — plus a 7-day debug artifact (`scrape-final-data`).
- The `notify` job now pulls its stats from that final artifact instead of an empty `main` checkout (previously it would have silently read from a nonexistent/empty DB).
- Added `permissions: contents: write` at the workflow level, required for `gh release create/upload/edit`.

## Other small fixes bundled in (found while working through this file)

- `.gitignore`: `*.db-shm` / `*.db-wal` / `*.db-journal` weren't ignored, so SQLite's WAL companion files (WAL mode was turned on in an earlier commit) could get swept up by a broad `git add`.
- `scripts/scrape_kinz.py`: the `--out` default was hardcoded to `/home/z/my-project/download/kinz_products.xlsx` — a path that only existed in a prior AI sandbox and isn't writable on a real machine, so the script would fail out of the box. Defaults to `data/kinz_products.xlsx` now.
- `scripts/build_scraper_reference_doc.py`: fixed a stale module docstring claiming the same broken default path (the actual `__main__` code already defaulted correctly to a relative path — only the comment was wrong).

## Test plan

- [x] `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/scrape.yml'))"` — valid YAML
- [ ] Not run end-to-end (no GitHub Actions runner in this environment) — recommend triggering via `workflow_dispatch` once merged to confirm the artifact handoff and release publish both work before the next scheduled Monday run.

## Notes for reviewer

- Nothing in `data/competitors_seed.json` or `CONTEXT.md`/`README.md` touched here — those are separate PRs.

v2.5.3 (Sep 6, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.3 Release Notes

The NumPy 2.5.3 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.2 release. Apart from the usual bug and maintenance work, there are a number of StringDType related fixes for problems discovered during the ongoing string work in the main branch.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15

Changes

  • Casting a fixed-width byte string array (np.bytes_) to StringDType now raises TypeError when the bytes are not valid UTF-8. Previously the invalid bytes were stored as-is and later caused undefined behavior in string operations.

    (gh-32296)

  • MaskedArray._fill_value would become stale when ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype. The mismatch was silent until something later called _check_fill_value, such as .view(), and then a TypeError would be raised. Now, when the copied fill_value is no longer valid for the new dtype, fall back to the default fill_value for that dtype instead of propagating the stale value. This may raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

    (gh-32423)

Contributors

A total of 9 people contributed to this release. People with a "+" by their names contributed a patch for the first time.

## What broke

The daily "Sentiment Alert" scheduled workflow (`.github/workflows/sentiment_alert.yml`) has been failing every run (e.g. [run 36139359712](https://github.com/nassim0014/btc-llm-sentiment/actions/runs/36139359712)):

```
smtp_port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", "587"))
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
```

`os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", "587")` only falls back to `"587"` when the key is **missing**. In this environment `SMTP_PORT` is present but set to an empty string (all SMTP/webhook secrets are unset), so the default never kicks in and the script crashes before it even reaches the "is email configured" check that would otherwise skip email delivery cleanly.

## Fix

`int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT") or "587")` — falls back to the default whether the variable is missing or blank.

## Verified

## What broke

The daily "Sentiment Alert" scheduled workflow (`.github/workflows/sentiment_alert.yml`) has been failing every run (e.g. [run 36139359712](https://github.com/nassim0014/btc-llm-sentiment/actions/runs/36139359712)):

```
smtp_port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", "587"))
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
```

`os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", "587")` only falls back to `"587"` when the key is **missing**. In this environment `SMTP_PORT` is present but set to an empty string (all SMTP/webhook secrets are unset), so the default never kicks in and the script crashes before it even reaches the "is email configured" check that would otherwise skip email delivery cleanly.

`int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT") or "587")` - falls back to the default whether the variable is missing or blank.

## Summary

Documentation-only. Files a new backlog item (item 12) in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`
for a red-CI root cause found during today's repo-review-loop sweep.

`main`'s `Docker build` and `Security scans` jobs have been red since
2026-09-10 (tracked as item 10), but the merge of dependabot PR #40
(`tensorflow-cpu` → `2.21.0`) surfaced a **new, different** root cause:
`requirements.txt` pins `shap==0.52.0`, which requires Python ≥3.12, while
`Dockerfile` hardcodes `ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.11`. `pip install -r
requirements.txt` now fails outright inside the build, and `pip-audit`
(the `Security scans` job) can't even compute a resolution plan for the
same reason.

This is the same "dependabot desync" pattern flagged before: individual
package bumps (`shap`, `tensorflow-cpu`, `numpy`, `pandas`) land one at a
time without verifying the resulting set is still mutually installable
against the pinned Docker Python version.

## Why a PR, not a direct push

This repo's `CLAUDE.md` rule 1 says "never push directly to `main` — open
a PR, squash-merge." An earlier review-loop run committed backlog items
directly to `main` (see `7bd515e4`, `3ae0bcde`) before that rule was
in force / noticed; following the current written rule here instead.

## Type of change

- [x] 📝 Documentation only — no application code touched

## What is NOT covered

This only documents the failure; it does not fix it. Item 12 lays out two
options for the owner (bump the Docker Python version to 3.12, or pin
`shap` back to a 3.11-compatible release) — this loop does not modify
`requirements.txt` or `Dockerfile` per its own review-only mandate.

Updates `transformers` from 4.44.2 to 5.10.1
Release notes

Sourced from transformers's releases.

Release v5.10.1

v5.10.0 was yanked as we publish on a corrupted branch. Sorry everyone, this happens when we rush a release!!!

New Model additions

Gemma4 unified+ Gemma4 MTP

Gemma 4 12B Unified is an encoder-free multimodal model with pretrained and instruction-tuned variants. Unlike standard Gemma 4, which uses dedicated encoder towers, Gemma 4 12B Unified projects raw inputs directly into the language model's embedding space through lightweight linear pipelines. This results in a simpler architecture while maintaining strong multimodal performance.

Key differences from standard Gemma 4:

  • No Vision Tower: Raw pixel patches are projected directly into LM space via a Dense + LayerNorm pipeline with factorized 2D positional embeddings, replacing the vision encoder.
  • No Audio Tower: Raw 16 kHz waveform samples are chunked into fixed-length frames and projected through a simple RMSNorm → Linear pipeline, replacing the mel spectrogram + Conformer encoder.
  • Shared Multimodal Pipeline: Both vision and audio use the same Gemma4UnifiedMultimodalEmbedder (RMSNorm → Linear) for the final projection to text hidden space.

You can find the original Gemma 4 12B Unified checkpoints under the Gemma 4 release.

  • who needs encoders? (#46385) by @douglas-reid @sgerrard @vasqu @molbap

Sapiens2

Sapiens2 is a family of high-resolution vision transformers pretrained on ~1 billion curated human images, designed for human-centric computer vision tasks including pose estimation, body-part segmentation, surface normal estimation, and pointmap estimation. The models scale from 0.4B to 5B parameters and train at native 1K resolution, with hierarchical 4K variants for extended spatial reasoning. Sapiens2 achieves substantial improvements over its predecessor with +4 mAP in pose estimation, +24.3 mIoU in body-part segmentation, and 45.6% error reduction in normal estimation.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Add Sapiens2 Model (#45919) by @guarin in #45919

DeepSeek-OCR-2

DeepSeek-OCR-2 is an OCR-specialized vision-language model built on a distinctive architecture that combines a SAM ViT-B vision encoder with a Qwen2 hybrid attention encoder, connected through an MLP projector to a DeepSeek-V2 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model. The model features a hybrid attention mechanism that applies bidirectional attention over image tokens and causal attention over query tokens, enabling efficient and accurate document understanding. It supports both plain OCR tasks and grounding capabilities with coordinate-aware output for document conversion to markdown format.

Links: Documentation

  • Add Deepseek-OCR-2 model (#45075) by @thisisiron in #45075

Mellum

Mellum is a code-focused Mixture-of-Experts language model developed by JetBrains. It is derived from the Qwen3-MoE architecture with per-layer-type RoPE and interleaved sliding window attention. The model has 12B total parameters with 2.5B active parameters per token, using 64 routed experts with 8 activated per token across 28 layers.

Links: Documentation

  • feat: Add support for JetBrains' Mellum v2 code generation model (#46112) by @shadeMe in #46112

Breaking changes

The Gemma4 vision pooler now casts inputs to float32 before scaling to prevent float16 overflow (inf saturation) with large checkpoints, which may cause minor numerical differences in outputs for users running Gemma-4 vision models in float16.

  • 🚨 Fix float16 overflow in Gemma4 vision pooler (#46277) by @Bluear7878

Audio Language Models (ALMs) now have a dedicated base model class without a language modeling head, aligning them with the design of Vision Language Models (VLMs); users relying on the previous model class structure should update their code to use the new base model class where appropriate.

  • 🚨 [ALM] Add base model without head (#45534) by @eustlb

PyTorch 2.13.0 Release Notes

  • Highlights

Highlights

For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release.

Tracked Regressions

ROCm wheels break torch.compile on CPU in environments without a GPU

Running a torch==2.13.0+rocm7.2 wheel in an environment where no GPU is available (torch.cuda.is_available() is False) breaks torch.compile on the CPU path: the first compile raises RuntimeError: Can't detect vectorized ISA for CPU (#189194). This is a regression from torch==2.12.1+rocm7.2, which compiles CPU code fine (detecting e.g. VecAVX2) in the same setup. The 2.13 ROCm wheel appears to rely on something present in the ROCm builder image to detect the CPU vectorized ISA, so it works when run on a ROCm image but fails on a plain CPU-only image.

Workaround: run the +rocm wheel on a ROCm image, or install a standard CPU/CUDA build for GPU-less environments.

Updates `transformers` from 4.44.2 to 5.10.1
Release notes

Sourced from transformers's releases.

Release v5.10.1

v5.10.0 was yanked as we publish on a corrupted branch. Sorry everyone, this happens when we rush a release!!!

New Model additions

Gemma4 unified+ Gemma4 MTP

Gemma 4 12B Unified is an encoder-free multimodal model with pretrained and instruction-tuned variants. Unlike standard Gemma 4, which uses dedicated encoder towers, Gemma 4 12B Unified projects raw inputs directly into the language model's embedding space through lightweight linear pipelines. This results in a simpler architecture while maintaining strong multimodal performance.

Key differences from standard Gemma 4:

  • No Vision Tower: Raw pixel patches are projected directly into LM space via a Dense + LayerNorm pipeline with factorized 2D positional embeddings, replacing the vision encoder.
  • No Audio Tower: Raw 16 kHz waveform samples are chunked into fixed-length frames and projected through a simple RMSNorm → Linear pipeline, replacing the mel spectrogram + Conformer encoder.
  • Shared Multimodal Pipeline: Both vision and audio use the same Gemma4UnifiedMultimodalEmbedder (RMSNorm → Linear) for the final projection to text hidden space.

You can find the original Gemma 4 12B Unified checkpoints under the Gemma 4 release.

  • who needs encoders? (#46385) by @douglas-reid @sgerrard @vasqu @molbap

Sapiens2

Sapiens2 is a family of high-resolution vision transformers pretrained on ~1 billion curated human images, designed for human-centric computer vision tasks including pose estimation, body-part segmentation, surface normal estimation, and pointmap estimation. The models scale from 0.4B to 5B parameters and train at native 1K resolution, with hierarchical 4K variants for extended spatial reasoning. Sapiens2 achieves substantial improvements over its predecessor with +4 mAP in pose estimation, +24.3 mIoU in body-part segmentation, and 45.6% error reduction in normal estimation.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Add Sapiens2 Model (#45919) by @guarin in #45919

DeepSeek-OCR-2

DeepSeek-OCR-2 is an OCR-specialized vision-language model built on a distinctive architecture that combines a SAM ViT-B vision encoder with a Qwen2 hybrid attention encoder, connected through an MLP projector to a DeepSeek-V2 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model. The model features a hybrid attention mechanism that applies bidirectional attention over image tokens and causal attention over query tokens, enabling efficient and accurate document understanding. It supports both plain OCR tasks and grounding capabilities with coordinate-aware output for document conversion to markdown format.

Links: Documentation

  • Add Deepseek-OCR-2 model (#45075) by @thisisiron in #45075

Mellum

Mellum is a code-focused Mixture-of-Experts language model developed by JetBrains. It is derived from the Qwen3-MoE architecture with per-layer-type RoPE and interleaved sliding window attention. The model has 12B total parameters with 2.5B active parameters per token, using 64 routed experts with 8 activated per token across 28 layers.

Links: Documentation

  • feat: Add support for JetBrains' Mellum v2 code generation model (#46112) by @shadeMe in #46112

Breaking changes

The Gemma4 vision pooler now casts inputs to float32 before scaling to prevent float16 overflow (inf saturation) with large checkpoints, which may cause minor numerical differences in outputs for users running Gemma-4 vision models in float16.

  • 🚨 Fix float16 overflow in Gemma4 vision pooler (#46277) by @Bluear7878

Audio Language Models (ALMs) now have a dedicated base model class without a language modeling head, aligning them with the design of Vision Language Models (VLMs); users relying on the previous model class structure should update their code to use the new base model class where appropriate.

  • 🚨 [ALM] Add base model without head (#45534) by @eustlb

Highlights

For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release.

Tracked Regressions

ROCm wheels break torch.compile on CPU in environments without a GPU

Running a torch==2.13.0+rocm7.2 wheel in an environment where no GPU is available (torch.cuda.is_available() is False) breaks torch.compile on the CPU path: the first compile raises RuntimeError: Can't detect vectorized ISA for CPU (#189194). This is a regression from torch==2.12.1+rocm7.2, which compiles CPU code fine (detecting e.g. VecAVX2) in the same setup. The 2.13 ROCm wheel appears to rely on something present in the ROCm builder image to detect the CPU vectorized ISA, so it works when run on a ROCm image but fails on a plain CPU-only image.

Workaround: run the +rocm wheel on a ROCm image, or install a standard CPU/CUDA build for GPU-less environments.

Backwards Incompatible Changes

  • Stop building CPython 3.13t (free-threaded) binaries (#182951)

    Upstream pypa/manylinux removed CPython 3.13t (free-threaded) on 2026-05-07, because 3.13t was experimental and has been superseded by the now-non-experimental CPython 3.14t. As a result, PyTorch 2.13 no longer ships cp313t wheels (Linux, Triton, and related artifacts). Users on the free-threaded interpreter should move to Python 3.14t.

## What changed

`docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` only — no code.

1. **Collapsed three stale "Now" items into one.** Former item 9, the
   un-numbered Docker item, and item 7 were all written around a
   `numpy==2.5.0` / `pandas==3.0.3` resolution deadlock. **That premise is
   gone** — PR #48 rolled `requirements.txt` back to `numpy==1.26.4` /
   `pandas==2.2.2`, and `pip install -r requirements.txt` now resolves
   cleanly on 3.11 and 3.12. They are replaced by a single **item 10** that
   states the blocker that is actually still true.

2. **Ticked off item 3.** It landed on `main` as **PR #46** (commit
   `4c7dd61`, merged 2026-09-01) — the `evaluate_oof_metrics` guard for
   `len(y_prob) < len(close) - 1`, which is the same gap the loop registry
   tracked as "item 8". Moved to Done with the correct PR number (the old
   Done entry said only "PR (2026-08-29)").

## Why

The registry notes for this repo explicitly flag that "backlog bookkeeping
has rotted before" here. Three overlapping items pointing at a resolved
root cause means the next 2–3 cycles re-investigate the same dead premise.
This PR makes the backlog say what's real: **`main` CI is red on two jobs,
and both now trace to CVE-laden `torch==2.4.1` / `transformers==4.44.2`
pins** whose fixes are breaking major upgrades (`transformers → 5.x`,
`torch → 2.9.x`) on the FinBERT-scoring / LSTM-training path — an owner
decision, and outside the closed loop's reach (`requirements*.txt` and
`.github/workflows/**` are both forbidden paths).

## Verified

| Check | Command | Result |
|-------|---------|--------|
| CI-red root cause | `gh run view 33899902889 --log` (latest `main` run) | Security scans: `pip-audit --strict` → "Found 82 known vulnerabilities in 7 packages", dominated by `transformers 4.44.2` + `torch 2.4.1`. Docker build: Trivy `unable to find the specified image` (build-push-action has no `load: true`). |
| Resolution premise is dead | read `requirements.txt` on `main` | pins `numpy==1.26.4`, `pandas==2.2.2` — resolves fine |
| Item 3 landed | `git log --oneline -- src/cv/walk_forward.py` + `gh pr list --state merged` | commit `4c7dd61` "guard evaluate_oof_metrics against y_prob shorter than close-1" = PR #46, merged 2026-09-01 |
| Test `test_fewer_probs_than_returns_does_not_crash` present | `grep -n` in `tests/test_backtest.py:246` | present |
| Baseline unaffected (docs-only) | `pytest tests/ -q` / `ruff check src/ scripts/ tests/` | **83 passed**, ruff **All checks passed!** |

## NOT covered

- The actual CI fix. `torch` / `transformers` upgrades + numeric
  re-validation of FinBERT scores and LSTM training are the owner's call;
  the `load: true` Docker one-liner is only worth doing bundled with that
  upgrade (the image carries the same CVEs, so Trivy fails either way).
- `requests 2.32.3 → 2.32.4` (2 minor advisories) — dependabot's queue.

Release notes

Sourced from plotly's releases.

v7.0.0

Fixed

  • Fix hex_to_rgb parsing of 3-digit shorthand hexadecimal colors such as #FFF [#5662], with thanks to @genrichez for the contribution!
  • Improve px.*_map() auto-fitting behavior when zoom and center are not specified [#5686]
  • Add <!doctype html> to the to_html() template to comply with modern web standards [#5693], with thanks to @mishrakushal for the contribution!
  • Apply histfunc/z aggregation to marginal_x/marginal_y="histogram" subplots in density_heatmap/density_contour, instead of always showing raw bin counts [#3521], with thanks to @lucasjamar for the contribution!
  • Fix mpl_to_plotly silently dropping matplotlib path collections in data coordinates (such as violin plots, pcolor, event plots, stack plots, fill_between, and stem plots) by rendering them as filled polygons or lines [#5702], with thanks to @robertoffmoura for the contribution!

Removed

  • Remove the deprecated Figure Factory functions create_2d_density, create_annotated_heatmap, create_bullet, create_candlestick, create_choropleth, create_distplot, create_facet_grid, create_gantt, create_hexbin_mapbox, create_ohlc, create_scatterplotmatrix, and create_violin [#5627]
  • Remove support for Kaleido versions less than v1.0.0 for static image generation [#5677]
  • Remove support for Orca for static image generation [#5677]
  • Remove engine argument from functions fig.write_image(),fig.to_image(), pio.write_image(), pio.write_images(), pio.to_image(), pio.full_figure_for_development(), and from renderer constructors [#5677]

Updated

  • Update plotly.js from version 3.6.0 to version 4.0.0 [#5673]. This is a major-version release with many changes. See the plotly.js release notes for the full list. The most significant changes include:
    • Add quiver trace type to visualize vector fields using arrows [#7710, #7945]
    • Add "Share Chart" modebar button for generating a chart-sharing link via Plotly Cloud [#7909]
    • Remove scattermapbox, choroplethmapbox, densitymapbox trace types, the mapbox subplot, and the mapboxAccessToken config option [#7860]. Use the equivalent *map traces instead.
      • The corresponding graph_objects and Plotly Express functions have also been removed in plotly.py; use the map versions instead
    • Drop support for MathJax v2, and add support for v4 [#7898]. MathJax is the JavaScript library used for rendering mathematical equations in plotly charts.
    • Switch color processing library from TinyColor to culori [#7536, #7962]. There are some changes to supported color string formats as a result:
      • rgb()/rgba() strings with decimal 0–1 fractions are no longer supported
      • hsv() color strings are no longer supported
      • Strings with invalid syntax such as hsl(120, 50% 50%) are no longer supported
      • New supported formats: '#ff0000aa', '#f00a', 'rgb(255 0 0)', 'rgba(255 0 0 / 0.5)', 'hsl(0 100% 50% / 0.5)', 'hsla(0, 100%, 50%, 0.5)', 'hwb(0, 0%, 0%)', lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch(), color(), hsl(0.5turn 60% 40%), hsl(none 60% 40%)
    • Replace country-regex with country-iso-search to search for country names in choropleth, scattergeo traces [#7856]. Most country names are handled exactly the same; a small number of legacy entries have been removed.
    • Change layout.geo.fitbounds default from false to 'locations' [#7895]. geo subplots will now auto-fit the initial view to the trace data by default.
    • Dynamically compute center and zoom values for scattermap and densitymap traces. The initial map view will now auto-fit to the trace data by default. Add layout.map.fitbounds attribute (default 'locations') to enable or disable auto-fitting behavior [#7884, #7913]
    • Fix GeoJSON bounding-box computation for choropleth and scattergeo traces whose geometry crosses the antimeridian [#7891]

  • Remove the deprecated Figure Factory functions create_2d_density, create_annotated_heatmap, create_bullet, create_candlestick, create_choropleth, create_distplot, create_facet_grid, create_gantt, create_hexbin_mapbox, create_ohlc, create_scatterplotmatrix, and create_violin [#5627]
  • Remove support for Kaleido versions less than v1.0.0 for static image generation [#5677]

  • Raise a clear ValueError when an unsupported marginal plot type is passed to Plotly Express, instead of failing later with a cryptic 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'constructor' message [#5625], with thanks to @eugen-goebel for the contribution!

Updated

  • Update plotly.js from version 3.6.0 to version 4.0.0-rc.0 [#5673]. This is a major-version release candidate with many changes. See the plotly.js release notes for the full list. The most significant changes include:

## Success criterion (written before implementing, verbatim)

> In `scripts/sentiment_alert.py`, `evaluate_alert()` gains a staleness guard: given a `now` timestamp and a `max_source_age_days` threshold (new `ALERT_MAX_SOURCE_AGE_DAYS` config constant), if the sentiment payload's `source_date` is older than `max_source_age_days` relative to `now`, `evaluate_alert()` must return a dict with `level == "STALE_DATA"` — never a directional level (`VERY_BULLISH`/`BULLISH`/`BEARISH`/`VERY_BEARISH`) — regardless of how extreme `daily_avg_sentiment` is. When `source_date` is within the freshness window, behavior is unchanged from before: normal threshold-based directional levels (or `None` for in-range sentiment) are returned exactly as today. A new test must load the OLD `evaluate_alert()` directly from the `main` branch via `git show` (a real base-commit pin, not a narrated claim) and prove that, given a sentiment payload whose `source_date` is 800 days old and whose `daily_avg_sentiment` is `0.5` (above the `very_bullish` threshold of `0.3`), the OLD code returns `level == "VERY_BULLISH"` (it has no staleness concept, so it fires a confident directional alert off 800-day-old data), while the NEW code, given the identical payload, returns `level == "STALE_DATA"`. A further test must show the NEW code still returns `level == "VERY_BULLISH"` for the same sentiment value when `source_date` is fresh (within the last 24 hours), unchanged from old behavior.

## What actually changed

```
scripts/sentiment_alert.py    |  45 ++++++++++++-
src/config.py                 |   7 ++
tests/test_sentiment_alert.py | 146 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
3 files changed, 196 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

- `evaluate_alert()` gains `now`/`max_source_age_days` keyword args and checks source freshness *before* the directional threshold logic; when stale it returns a new `STALE_DATA` alert instead.
- `src/config.py` gains `ALERT_MAX_SOURCE_AGE_DAYS = 2` (documented).
- `tests/test_sentiment_alert.py` (new, 6 tests) pins the OLD `evaluate_alert()` straight from `main` via `git show` and proves it fires `VERY_BULLISH` on an 800-day-old, +0.5-sentiment payload, while the new code returns `STALE_DATA` for the same input and is unchanged on fresh data. A follow-up commit made the base-commit pin resolve against `main`/`origin/main` and skip cleanly (instead of erroring) on a shallow CI checkout, after the verifier found this repo's CI test job doesn't fetch `main` — see verdict below.

**Why this is real, not theoretical:** `Data/cryptonews.csv`'s newest row is `2023-12-19` — about 990 days old as of today. The daily `sentiment_alert.yml` cron has been capable of firing a confident directional alert off that frozen data indefinitely, with nothing distinguishing it from a live signal.

**Local verification:** 89 tests pass (was 83, +6 new). `ruff check src/ scripts/ tests/` clean. `bandit -r src/ scripts/ -ll -ii -x tests/` clean.

## Branch

`exp/2026-09-05/sentiment-alert-staleness-guard`

## Independent verification — VERIFIED

An independent Opus-based verifier was given only the repo path, the diff, and the success criterion above (verbatim) — no framing, no argument for the change, and no knowledge of who wrote it. It was instructed to try to refute the claim and default to REFUTED if uncertain. Its full verdict:

> **VERDICT: VERIFIED**
>
> Every clause of the success criterion holds, and I confirmed the central behavioral delta independently rather than trusting the test. Several real defects exist around the edges; none contradict the criterion as written.
>
> **Evidence:**
> 1. Diff matches reality — confirmed against the actual files in the repo.
> 2. Premise confirmed independently: `git show main:scripts/sentiment_alert.py` shows the old `evaluate_alert(sentiment_data: dict)` signature has no `now`/`max_source_age_days` and no staleness logic at all — the bug is real, not narrated.
> 3. The base-commit pin is genuine, not fake — replicated the loader outside pytest, confirmed the old module is a distinct object with `check=True` (a missing ref would raise, not silently pass), and confirmed old vs. new diverge *only* on the staleness axis: old code returns `VERY_BULLISH` on the 800-day-stale payload, new code returns `STALE_DATA`; both agree (`VERY_BULLISH`) on the fresh payload.
> 4. Tests pass and nothing regressed: `tests/test_sentiment_alert.py` → 6 passed; full suite on the branch → 89 passed; full suite on `main` → 83 passed (exactly +6, no regressions); `ruff check` → all checks passed.
> 5. Downstream pipeline is safe — the `STALE_DATA` dict's key set is identical to the directional dict's, so `send_email_alert`/`send_slack_alert`/`send_discord_alert`/`log_alert` all handle it without crashing.
> 6. The premise is materially live in production: `Data/cryptonews.csv` spans through 2023-12-19, ~990 days stale as of today.
>
> **Defects found (reported, not criterion violations):**
> 1. *(Highest priority, already fixed in a follow-up commit on this branch)* CI's test job checks out with no `fetch-depth: 0`, so `main` may not exist as a ref on a PR-triggered run — the original pin would have errored red rather than passing or skipping. Fixed by resolving against `main`/`origin/main` with a clean skip if neither resolves.
> 2. The base-commit test still skips silently (with a clear reason) on a `.git`-less tree (e.g. a tarball).
> 3. `source_date` that's unparseable (`NaT` after `errors="coerce"`) falls through to directional logic — fails open rather than treating unparseable-as-stale.
> 4. A future-dated `source_date` (negative age) also bypasses the guard.
> 5. A payload missing `source_date` entirely with in-range sentiment now raises `KeyError` where old code returned `None` on that path.
> 6. A naive (non-tz-aware) `now` passed by a caller raises `TypeError` (offset-aware vs. offset-naive datetime subtraction) — untested.
> 7. The boundary is strict (`age_days > max`, not `>=`) — an exactly-2.00-day-old source is treated as fresh; undocumented and untested.

**Not fixed in this PR:** defects 3–7 above are real edge cases the literal criterion doesn't cover, and fixing all of them would grow this from a small, focused guard into a larger validation rewrite. Flagging them here for a follow-up rather than scope-creeping this PR. Defect 1 (the CI-breaking one) *was* fixed, since it would have broken this PR's own CI check for a reason unrelated to the feature.

## PR status

Parked for review — **this loop has no merge authority and will never merge this itself.** Verdict is VERIFIED; this is ready for a human look.

items.old:
## Problem

`requirements.txt` is **unresolvable on `main`** — `pip install -r requirements.txt` fails with `ResolutionImpossible`. This is why CI is red:
- **Docker build** fails (`pip install -r requirements.txt` → exit 1).
- **Security scan** (`pip-audit`) can't resolve the env to audit it.

The test job stays green only because it installs a small *unpinned* subset (`numpy pandas scikit-learn pytest ...`) without torch/TF, so it never hits the conflict.

## Root cause

Dependabot bumped individual packages past what the un-bumped heavy ML anchors allow:

| Bumped | Anchor it conflicts with |
|---|---|
| `numpy==2.5.0` | `tensorflow-cpu==2.17.0` needs `numpy<2.0.0` |
| `shap==0.52.0` (needs `numpy>=2`) | direct contradiction with tensorflow-cpu |
| `pandas==3.0.3` | `streamlit==1.39.0` needs `pandas<3` |

## Fix (verified)

Roll the three over-bumps back to versions consistent with the anchors:
- `numpy` 2.5.0 → **1.26.4**
- `pandas` 3.0.3 → **2.2.2**
- `shap` 0.52.0 → **0.46.0**

`pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt` now **resolves cleanly** (the full stack co-installs) → fixes the Docker build and restores a reproducible, installable environment.

## Not fixed here (separate decision) ⚠️

`pip-audit` will still flag transitive **`protobuf 4.25.9`** (fix `≥5.29`) — but that's **locked `<5` by `tensorflow-cpu==2.17.0`** — and **`pillow 10.4.0`**. Clearing the audit fully needs a deliberate **tensorflow-cpu upgrade** (Keras 3 / model-reproducibility implications), which is a maintainer call, not a safe drive-by. So the **Docker build** job goes green with this PR; the **Security scan** job needs that follow-up.

Longer term: group Dependabot ML bumps (or pin the anchors) so a single-package bump can't desync the stack again.

## What changed

`evaluate_oof_metrics` (`src/cv/walk_forward.py`) aligns the trading
`signal` with per-day `rets` before computing the strategy return series.
That alignment only handled `len(signal) > len(rets)` — it truncated the
signal. The opposite case, `len(y_prob) < len(close) - 1`, fell straight
into `strat_rets = signal * rets` and raised:

```
ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (2,) (4,)
```

The alignment is now symmetric: both arrays are trimmed to their common
prefix (`common = min(len(signal), len(rets))`).

For the normal path (`len(y_prob) == len(close_va)`, so `len(signal) ==
len(rets) + 1`) the behaviour is identical to before — signal is trimmed
by one element, returns unchanged. Only the previously-crashing branch
changes.

## Why

Backlog item 3 asked for degenerate-input coverage of
`evaluate_oof_metrics`. Three of its four branches (empty, single-element,
zero-std) already shipped in PR #33. The "mismatched lengths" branch was
half-covered: `test_mismatched_lengths_fees_skipped` only exercises
signal-longer-than-returns. This closes the other direction.

This is **not a live crash** — `run_walk_forward` always passes
`len(y_prob) == len(close_va)`, so the mismatch is only reachable with
hand-constructed inputs. But the function already defends the other
direction, so the asymmetry was almost certainly unintended.

## Verified

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` → **83 passed** (was 82), 5 pre-existing warnings
- `.venv/bin/ruff check src/ scripts/ tests/` → **All checks passed!**
- `.venv/bin/bandit -r src/cv/walk_forward.py -ll -ii` → **No issues identified**
- Regression test proven: reverting the guard makes
  `test_fewer_probs_than_returns_does_not_crash` fail with the
  `ValueError` above; restoring it passes.
- Env: Python 3.12, `pip install numpy pandas scikit-learn pytest pytest-cov ruff bandit`
  (the lightweight CI install per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

## Not covered / out of scope

- **CI baseline is already red on `main`** (independent of this PR):
  `Security scans` (pip-audit) and `Docker build` both fail because
  `requirements.txt` is `ResolutionImpossible` — `shap==0.52.0` needs
  `numpy>=2`, `tensorflow-cpu==2.17.0` needs `numpy<2.0.0`. This PR does
  not touch that; the backlog's 🔴 Docker item and item 7 are updated
  with the real root cause. Expect this PR's `Security scans` / `Docker
  build` checks to stay red for that pre-existing reason; `Test (3.11)`,
  `Test (3.12)` and `ML import smoke` are the relevant checks here.
- No change to metric values for any valid input.
- `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`: ticked off items 1 & 2 (merged long ago in
  PR #23 / #24, never recorded) and trimmed item 3 to what remained.

Loop-Agent: closed-loop / claude / laptop

Bumps [optuna](https://github.com/optuna/optuna) from 3.6.1 to 4.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from optuna's releases.

v4.9.0

This is the release note of v4.9.0.

Highlights

Enhance Multi-Objective Constrained Parallel Optimization in GPSampler

@sawa3030 introduces parallelization enhancements to GPSampler, leveraging the Kriging Believer approach for constrained and multi-objective optimization (#6481). This improvement allows for more efficient exploration when multiple trials are running concurrently.

The GP surrogate is updated by assigning temporary objective function values to the running trials.

For more technical details and benchmarks, please check out our blog post: Improving Optuna’s GPSampler Parallelization by Considering Running Trials.

Deprecate Several Features

The following features are deprecated in v4.9.0 and scheduled for removal in v6.0.0.

optuna

  • Several arguments in TPESampler (#6635)
    • prior_weight, consider_magic_clip, consider_endpoints, gamma, weights, hyperopt_parameters: These internal parameters are being deprecated to simplify the interface, as the default settings are optimal for most use cases.
    • warn_independent_sampling: Deprecated because TPESampler now robustly supports both independent and joint sampling, making this warning obsolete.
    • categorical_distance_func: This advanced feature will be migrated to OptunaHub in the future.
  • x0 and sigma0 options in CmaEsSampler (#6624)
    • These options have been deprecated because they require a deep understanding of CmaEsSampler's internals to be configured effectively.
  • optuna.terminator module (#6668)
    • This feature will be migrated to OptunaHub in the future.
  • RetryFailedTrialCallback (#6670)
    • This class has been renamed to RetryHeartbeatStaleTrialCallback to better reflect its behavior and avoid confusion with general trial retries (#6085).
  • optuna.integration module
    • The optuna.integration module currently acts as a shortcut to the external optuna_integration package for backward compatibility. Please import directly from the optuna_integration package going forward.

optuna-integration

  • PyCmaSampler: Please use Optuna's native CmaEsSampler instead.
  • CometCallback: This feature will be migrated to OptunaHub in the future.
  • MLflowCallback: This feature will be migrated to OptunaHub in the future.
  • TensorBoardCallback: This feature will be migrated to OptunaHub in the future.
  • TrackioCallback: This feature will be migrated to OptunaHub in the future.
  • WeightsAndBiasesCallback: This class has already been migrated to OptunaHub.

Breaking Changes

  • Deprecate PyCmaSampler (optuna/optuna-integration#276)
  • Add deprecation message for CometCallback (optuna/optuna-integration#280)
  • Add deprecation message for MLflowCallback (optuna/optuna-integration#281)

Bumps [plotly](https://github.com/plotly/plotly.py) from 5.24.1 to 6.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from plotly's releases.

v6.9.0

Fixed

  • Raise a clear ValueError when an unsupported marginal plot type is passed to Plotly Express, instead of failing later with a cryptic 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'constructor' message [#5625], with thanks to @eugen-goebel for the contribution!

Updated

  • Update plotly.js from version 3.6.0 to version 3.7.0. See the plotly.js release notes for more information [#5639]. Notable changes include:
    • Rename sendDataToCloud modebar button to sendChartToCloud, and update to upload chart to Plotly Cloud [#7802, #7852, #7854]. NOTE: The Plotly Cloud endpoint for receiving charts is not yet functional, so this button won't complete the upload.
    • Fix stale scattergl error bars after toggling traces with mixed error bar visibility [#7773], with thanks to @JulienIcon for the contribution!
    • Fix geo fitbounds to choose a compact longitude range when point data straddles the antimeridian [#7837], with thanks to @SharadhNaidu for the contribution!

Full Changelog: https://github.com/plotly/plotly.py/compare/v6.8.0...v6.9.0

v6.8.0

Added

  • Add optional font parameter for make_subplots [#5393], with thanks to @Zomtir for the contribution!

Fixed

  • Fix issue where user-specified color_continuous_scale was ignored when template had autocolorscale=True [#5439], with thanks to @antonymilne for the contribution!
  • Use presence of COLAB_NOTEBOOK_ID env var to enable Colab renderer instead of testing import of google.colab [#5473], with thanks to @kevineger for the contribution!
  • Fix incorrect annotation placement for add_vline, add_hline, add_vrect, and add_hrect on datetime axes [#5508], with thanks to @mosh3eb for the contribution!
  • Update tests to be compatible with numpy 2.4 [#5522], with thanks to @thunze for the contribution!
  • Fix issue where js/ directory was unintentionally installed as a top-level Python package when installing plotly [#5587]
  • Add default headers to be passed in to Kaleido v1.3.0 to avoid blocked Open Street Map tiles [#5588]
  • Propagate the requested default_height/default_width to the outer wrapper div produced by to_html so that responsive (percentage) dimensions inherit from a sized parent container instead of collapsing to the plotly.js 450px fallback [#5591], with thanks to @SharadhNaidu for the contribution!

Updated

  • The __eq__ method for graph_objects classes now returns NotImplemented to give the other operand an opportunity to handle the comparison [#5547], with thanks to @RazerM for the contribution!
  • Update plotly.js from version 3.5.0 to version 3.6.0. See the plotly.js release notes for more information [#5608]. Notable changes include:
    • Add support for arrays for the pie property legendrank, so that it can be configured per slice [#7723]
    • Add hoversort layout attribute to sort unified hover label items by value [#7734]

v6.7.0

Added

  • Add facet_row support to px.imshow for creating subplots along an additional dimension [#5445], with thanks to @FBumann for the contribution!

Fixed

  • Update numpy.percentile syntax to stop using deprecated alias [#5483], with thanks to @Mr-Neutr0n for the contribution!
    • numpy with a version less than 1.22 is no longer supported.
  • Handle empty px.histogram by skipping None label in hover template [#5535], with thanks to @tysoncung for the contribution!

Updated

  • Update plotly.js from version 3.4.0 to version 3.5.0. See the plotly.js release notes for more information. [#5565]. Notable changes include:
    • Add hoveranywhere and clickanywhere layout attributes to enable emitting hover and click events anywhere in the plot area, not just over traces [#7707]
    • Add displayNotifier configuration property to set the display of notifier in the top right area of the viewport [#7730]
    • Update USA location lookup for scattergeo and choropleth traces to use both location names and abbreviations [#7731]

v6.6.0

Fixed

  • Remove unneeded type="text/javascript" attribute from <style> tag [#5454], with thanks to @hannob for the contribution!

Sourced from plotly's releases.

  • Raise a clear ValueError when an unsupported marginal plot type is passed to Plotly Express, instead of failing later with a cryptic 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'constructor' message [#5625], with thanks to @eugen-goebel for the contribution!

Updated
