## Summary

A full-repo audit (3 parallel explorations + direct file reads) found this boilerplate is **substantially real** — most `lib/` modules and app routes are genuine, working implementations, not a vaporware README. But it surfaced a specific list of correctness bugs, silently-stubbed "shipped" features, and doc/reality drift. This PR fixes what's in scope for a correctness-and-hygiene pass; larger architectural items (Cloudflare compatibility, the Tailwind v4 upgrade, major Dependabot bumps) are called out but intentionally left for their own dedicated passes.

## Critical fix

- **Subscription-creation FK bug**: `reconcileSubscription()`'s `create` branch hardcoded `planId: "default-plan-id"` — not a real seeded UUID. The **first Stripe webhook for any new paying org would throw an FK-constraint error and never recover** (Stripe retries forever, subscription never activates). Fixed by adding `stripePriceIdMonthly/Yearly` to `Plan`, resolving the real plan from the subscription's Stripe price ID (`getPlanByStripePriceId`), and making `reconcileSubscription()` require a real `planId` — no more silent fallback. `customer.subscription.deleted` (which never had plan info) now goes through a new `markSubscriptionStatus()` instead.

## Other correctness fixes

- Wired the GDPR compliance page's Export/Delete buttons — they had **no `onClick`/`action` at all**, despite `lib/gdpr/export.ts` and `deletion.ts` being fully implemented.
- Migrated `.eslintrc.json` → `eslint.config.mjs` (ESLint 9 flat config). The legacy config was already known-broken (see commit history: `continue-on-error: true` was added to CI's lint step as a workaround, so lint has been enforcing nothing).
- Fixed `/api/livez` + `/api/readyz` — only a single `/api/health/route.ts` existed, trying to branch on `req.url.pathname.endsWith("/ready")`, which is dead code (Next.js only routes exact-path requests to a `route.ts`). `/api/health` kept as a liveness alias.
- Cleaned up a couple of pre-existing dead imports (`stripe`, `prisma`, unused `session` var) that would fail lint once `--max-warnings=0` is actually enforced.

## Wired up two previously-stubbed "shipped" features

- **Budget-threshold alerts**: `alertBudgetThreshold()` only ever did `console.warn` with a comment saying it was "stubbed pending Phase 3" — but Phase 3 shipped a complete webhook dispatcher it never used. Now dispatches a real `usage.budget_threshold` webhook event.
- **GDPR export**: produced a raw JSON blob with its own comment admitting "in production, ZIP this" — README/CHANGELOG explicitly advertise "ZIP export". Now uses `jszip` (pure JS, no native binary) to build a real `.zip` with one file per data category.

## Security hardening

- Added `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` RLS policies (`supabase/migrations/0005_rls_write_policies.sql`) — only `SELECT` policies existed before. Also found and fixed: `invitations` had RLS **enabled with zero policies at all** (not even SELECT), which under real enforcement means the table was completely inaccessible.
- Deliberately did **not** add user-writable policies for `audit_logs`, `billing_events`, `token_usage`, `subscriptions`, `usage_records`, `webhook_events` — those are system-of-record tables; giving users direct write access would be a regression.
- Strengthened the `.env.example` RLS-bypass warning and cross-referenced it from `docs/SECURITY.md`.

## Real test suite

No test files existed anywhere on `main` despite `context.md` mandating tests for billing/RBAC/cost-metering code and the README claiming Vitest coverage (`--passWithNoTests` was masking this). Added `vitest.config.ts` + real tests:
- `src/lib/auth/permissions.test.ts` — RBAC wildcard/domain/role scoping
- `src/lib/webhooks/signer.test.ts` — HMAC sign/verify round-trip, tamper + wrong-length rejection
- `src/lib/billing/webhooks.test.ts` — **regression test for the FK bug fix** (asserts a real `planId` flows through, not `"default-plan-id"`)
- `src/lib/ai/cost.test.ts` — billing-period date math

## Hygiene

- Removed a leaked 46KB AI-agent session transcript at `tool-results/` (exposed local absolute paths, internal git workflow) + gitignored the directory.
- `context.md` (the repo's own "single source of truth" for AI agents) said Phase 3 was still PENDING and "Repo: TBD" — corrected to match reality, added an Amendment Log entry per the file's own append-only convention.
- Fixed `docs/SECURITY.md`'s vulnerability-report email to match the README's actual contact address.
- Clarified `pnpm-workspace.yaml` isn't a monorepo config (no `packages:` field — it's pnpm's build-script allowlist).
- Expanded `docs/DEPLOYMENT-CLOUDFLARE.md`'s vague "some Node.js modules may not work" into a specific callout: `argon2` and Prisma's default engine are very likely incompatible with Workers, and the Cloudflare tooling isn't even pinned in `package.json`. **Not fixing this** — it's a real architecture change (driver adapters, swapping the hash) out of scope here; Cloudflare is now clearly marked experimental/unverified rather than presented as solved.

## Explicitly out of scope this pass

- The Tailwind v3→v4 migration (Dependabot PR #7) — real breaking-change migration, `context.md`'s claim corrected to say v3.4 (actual) instead.
- Major Dependabot bumps (Prisma 6→7, TypeScript 5→6, Stripe 17→22, `@ai-sdk/*` 1.x→4.x, `lint-staged`, `tailwind-merge`) — real API changes needing their own regression pass. Safe patch/minor ones (`@radix-ui/react-switch`, `tsx`, `actions/setup-node`) will be merged separately once this PR is green.
- Actually fixing Cloudflare compatibility (vs. documenting the risk) — see above.

## Verification

- [ ] CI (`build` / `test` / `security` jobs) green on this PR
- [ ] Once `pnpm lint` is confirmed clean in CI, will push a follow-up commit removing `continue-on-error: true` from the CI lint step so it actually gates again
- Manually traced: `reconcileSubscription()` is never called without a resolvable `planId` anywhere in the Stripe webhook route

Release notes

Sourced from prisma's releases.

7.8.0

Today, we are excited to share the 7.8.0 stable release 🎉

🌟 Star this repo for notifications about new releases, bug fixes & features — or follow us on X!

Highlights

ORM

Features

Prisma Client

  • Added a queryPlanCacheMaxSize option to the PrismaClient constructor for fine-grained control over the query plan cache. Pass 0 to disable the cache entirely, or omit it to use the default cache size. A larger value can improve performance in applications that execute many unique queries, while a smaller one can reduce memory usage. (#29503)

Bug Fixes

Prisma Client

  • Fixed an equality filter panic and incorrect ::jsonb cast when filtering on PostgreSQL JSON list columns. Queries using where: { jsonListField: { equals: [...] } }prisma/prisma-engines#5804
  • Fixed case-insensitive JSON field filtering (mode: insensitive), allowing where: { jsonField: { equals: "...", mode: "insensitive" } }prisma/prisma-engines#5806
  • Fixed incorrect parameterization of enum values that have a custom database name set via @map. (#29422)
  • Fixed a database parameter limit check (P2029), which could incorrectly reject or miss over-limit queries. (#29422)
  • Fixed a regression that caused missing SQL Server VARCHARprisma/prisma-engines#5801

Schema Engine

  • Fixed a misleading error message in prisma migrate diff that referenced the --shadow-database-url CLI flag, which was removed in Prisma 7. (#29455)
  • Fixed prisma migrate dev (and shadow database migration replay in general) failing with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction blockprisma/prisma-engines#5799
  • Fixed PostgreSQL introspection silently dropping sequence defaults when the database returns the schema-qualified form pg_catalog.nextval('sequence_name'::regclass) instead of the bare nextval(...). Columns backed by sequences now correctly appear as @default(autoincrement())prisma/prisma-engines#5802

Driver Adapters

  • @prisma/adapter-d1: Savepoint operations (createSavepoint, rollbackToSavepoint, releaseSavepoint) now silently no-op with debug logging instead of executing SQL statements, consistent with how the D1 adapter already treats top-level transactions. (#29499)

Open roles at Prisma

Interested in joining Prisma? We're growing and have several exciting opportunities across the company for developers who are passionate about building with Prisma. Explore our open positions on our Careers page and find the role that's right for you.

Enterprise support

Thousands of teams use Prisma and many of them already tap into our Enterprise & Agency Support Program for hands-on help with everything from schema integrations and performance tuning to security and compliance.

With this program you also get priority issue triage and bug fixes, expert scalability advice, and custom training so that your Prisma-powered apps stay rock-solid at any scale. Learn more or join: https://prisma.io/enterprise.

Today, we are excited to share the 7.7.0 stable release 🎉

🌟 Star this repo for notifications about new releases, bug fixes & features — or follow us on X!

## Summary

Task 3 of 5 — adds the ability to edit an existing agent's name, description, system prompt, model, temperature, and max tokens. The agent detail page was previously read-only.

## Changes

**`src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/actions.ts`** (new) — `updateAgentAction` server action:
- RBAC-gated on `agents:update` (ADMIN+, already in `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`).
- Reuses the existing-but-unused `updateAgentSchema` (`createAgentSchema.partial()`).
- Verifies the agent belongs to the org and that any new `modelConfigId` exists.
- Writes an `UPDATE` audit log, then `revalidatePath` + redirect back to the detail page.

**`src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/edit/page.tsx`** (new) — server component that loads the agent + model configs and renders `EditAgentForm`. `notFound()` if the agent doesn't exist or has no model config.

**`src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/edit-form.tsx`** (new) — pre-filled form mirroring the create form (`name`, `description`, `modelConfigId` `<select>`, `systemPrompt` `<textarea>`, `temperature`, `maxTokens`). Posts `agentId` as a hidden field. Reuses the same shadcn `<Input>`/`<Label>`/`<Button>` styling as `agents/new`.

**`src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx`** — adds an **Edit** button (outline variant) next to Chat, linking to `/dashboard/agents/<id>/edit`.

## Approach
Minimal new surface: reuses `updateAgentSchema` (already defined as the placeholder for this), the create-form layout, and the existing `agents:update` RBAC entry. **No schema changes, no new validators.**

## Verification
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` — clean

## Manual test (recommended)
1. Sign in as an ADMIN/OWNER.
2. Open an agent's detail page → click **Edit**.
3. Change a field (e.g. name + temperature) → **Save Changes**.
4. Confirm you're redirected back to the detail page with the new values, and an `UPDATE` audit log row was written.
5. Sign in as a MEMBER/VIEWER → the action should throw `FORBIDDEN` (members have `agents:read`/`agents:create` but not `agents:update`).

## Summary

Task 1 of 5 — clicking a past conversation in the chat sidebar now loads its real messages into the chat window instead of clearing it. Deep links from the agent detail page (`/dashboard/chat?conversation=<id>`, `?agent=<id>`) also now work.

## Problem
Previously, clicking a past conversation only set the selected id and wiped the visible messages (`setMessages([])`). Users saw an empty chat for a conversation that did have messages in the DB. The actual messages only re-entered the conversation when the user sent a *new* message.

## Changes

**`src/app/dashboard/chat/page.tsx`** (server component): reads `searchParams`; when `?conversation=` is present, verifies the conversation belongs to `(orgId, userId)`, fetches its messages (role USER/ASSISTANT, asc, limit 50), maps to `{ id, role, content, createdAt }`; passes `initialAgentId`, `initialConversationId`, `initialMessages` to `<ChatInterface>`.

**`src/components/chat/chat-interface.tsx`** (client component): seeds `useChat({ initialMessages })`; `handleSelectConversation` now does `router.push("/dashboard/chat?conversation=<id>")` instead of `setMessages([])`.

## Approach
Server component + Prisma for reads (matches existing patterns). No new API routes, no schema changes. Role-lowercasing mirrors `src/app/api/chat/route.ts`.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) — clean
- `pnpm lint` — pre-existing tooling issue unrelated to this change (ESLint 9 + legacy eslintrc; `next lint` breaks on the space in the path). Fails identically on `main`.

items.old:
## What this PR does

Builds out every missing page in the app — 14 new routes + 2 new components. The app goes from a partial scaffold to a fully navigable, production-shaped SaaS.

### Critical fix
`src/config/nav.ts` had every nav link missing the `/dashboard` prefix. That's why `/agents` returned 404 — the link should have been `/dashboard/agents`. Fixed.

### New pages (14)
- **`/dashboard/chat`** — Full streaming AI chat UI (the core feature). Uses `@ai-sdk/react` `useChat` hook. Agent selector, conversation sidebar, message bubbles, streaming responses, auto-scroll, error handling.
- **`/dashboard/agents/[id]`** — Agent detail: model config, generation params, system prompt, recent conversations.
- **`/dashboard/agents`** — Rewritten to show real agent cards from the DB.
- **`/dashboard/settings/general`** — Org name editing (Server Action), current plan, member list.
- **`/dashboard/settings/members`** — Active members + pending invitations.
- **`/dashboard/settings/billing`** — Current plan, upgrade cards, billing event history.
- **`/dashboard/settings/api-keys`** — API key list with prefixes, last-used, status.
- **`/dashboard/settings/webhooks`** — Webhook endpoints with delivery counts.
- **`/dashboard/settings/audit-log`** — Immutable audit trail with color-coded actions.
- **`/dashboard/settings/compliance`** — GDPR data export + right-to-erasure.
- **`/dashboard/knowledge-base`** — KB cards with document counts.
- **`/onboarding`** — New user flow: create first org (Server Action creates org + owner membership + trial subscription).
- **`/pricing`** — Public pricing page with all 4 plans.

### New components
- `src/components/chat/chat-interface.tsx` — Client component for streaming AI chat.
- `src/components/dashboard/org-switcher.tsx` — Client component for multi-org switching.

### Dashboard layout
- Added org switcher to header (dropdown if user has >1 org).
- Added user avatar with email initial.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` — passes (0 errors)
- `pnpm build` — passes (22 routes in build output)

## To test locally
```bash
git checkout origin/feat/full-app-buildout -- .
pnpm dev
# Visit http://localhost:3000/dashboard — all nav links work now
# Visit http://localhost:3000/dashboard/chat — chat UI loads
```

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.0.8

Patch Changes

  • #1809 179b437 - Fix lint-staged discarding the ongoing merge conflict status (.git/MERGE_HEAD) when using the --hide-unstaged or --hide-all options.

  • #1811 3d0b2c0 - Fix issues with Git commands that are successful but also emit warnings to stderr, by ignoring the stderr output completely when the process exits with code 0. This was the behavior when using nano-spawn and execa, but when switching to tinyexec in 16.3.0 both stdout and stderr were used as interleaved output.

v17.0.7

Patch Changes

  • #1806 e692e58 - Update dependency tinyexec@^1.2.4.

v17.0.6

Patch Changes

  • #1803 bdf2770 - Run all tests with Deno, in addition to Node.js and Bun.

  • #1796 7508272 - Fix performance regression of lint-staged v17 by going back to using git add to stage task modifications. This was changed to git update-index --again in v17 for less manual work, but unfortunately the update-index command gets slower in very large Git repos.

  • #1797 7b2505a - This version of lint-staged uses the new staged publishing for npm packages feature. Releases are already published from GitHub Actions with trusted publishing, but now an additional approval with two-factor authentication is also required.

  • #1802 321b0a9 - Downgrade dependency tinyexec@1.2.2 to avoid issues in version 1.2.3.

v17.0.5

Patch Changes

  • #1792 1f67271 - Correctly set the --max-arg-length default value based on the running platform. This controls how very long lists of staged files are split into multiple chunks.

v17.0.4

Patch Changes

  • #1788 f95c1f8 - Another fix for making sure lint-staged adds task modifications correctly to the commit in the following cases:

    • after editing <file> it is staged with git add <file>, and then committed with git commit
    • after editing <file> it is committed with git commit --all without explicit git add
    • after editing <file> it is committed with git commit <pathspec> without explicit git add

    There's new test cases which actually setup the Git pre_commit hook to run lint-staged and verify them. These issues started in v17.0.0 when trying to improve support for committig without having explicitly staged files.

Release notes

Sourced from tailwindcss's releases.

v4.3.2

Fixed

  • Support bare spacing values for auto-rows-* and auto-cols-* utilities (e.g. auto-rows-12 and auto-cols-16) (#20229)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode from crashing on Windows when @source points to a directory that doesn't exist (#20242)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing in Deno v2.8.x when context.parentURL is not a valid URL (#20245)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode rebuilds when the input CSS file changes in an ignored directory (#20246)
  • Allow @variant rules used in addBase(…) to use custom variants defined later (#20247)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing during HMR when scanned files or directories are deleted (#20259)
  • Generate font-size instead of color declarations for text-[--spacing(…)] (#20260)
  • Prevent @source patterns from scanning unrelated sibling files and folders (#20263)
  • Extract class candidates adjacent to Template Toolkit delimiters like %]…[% in .tt, .tt2, and .tx files (#20269)
  • Extract class candidates from conditional Maud syntax like p.text-black[condition] (#20269)
  • Prevent @position-try rules from triggering unknown at-rule warnings when optimizing CSS (#20277)
  • Support class suggestions for named opacity modifiers from --opacity theme values (#20287)
  • Prevent type errors in @tailwindcss/postcss when used with newer PostCSS patch releases (#20289)

v4.3.1

Added

  • Add --silent option to suppress output in @tailwindcss/cli (#20100)

Fixed

  • Remove deprecation warnings by using Module#registerHooks instead of Module#register on Node 26+ (#20028)
  • Canonicalization: don't crash when plugin utilities throw for unsupported values (#20052)
  • Allow @apply to be used with CSS mixins (#19427)
  • Ensure not-* correctly negates @container queries, including style(…) queries (#20059)
  • Ensure drop-shadow-* color utilities work with custom shadow values containing calc(…) (#20080)
  • Fix 'Sourcemap is likely to be incorrect' warnings when using @tailwindcss/vite (#20103)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/webpack can be installed in Rspack projects without requiring webpack as a peer dependency (#20027)
  • Canonicalization: don't suggest invalid calc(…) expressions (e.g. px-[calc(1rem+0px)] → px-[calc(1rem+0)]) (#20127)
  • Canonicalization: avoid suggesting large spacing-scale values for arbitrary lengths (e.g. left-[99999px] → left-[99999px], not left-24999.75) (#20130)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode recovers when a tracked dependency is deleted and restored (#20137)
  • Ensure standalone @tailwindcss/cli binaries are ignored when scanning for class candidates (#20139)
  • Ensure class candidates are extracted from Twig addClass(…) and removeClass(…) calls (#20198)
  • Don't crash in the Ruby or Vue preprocessors when scanning files containing invalid UTF-8 bytes (#19588)
  • Allow @variant to be used inside addBase (#19480)
  • Ensure @source globs with symlinks are preserved (#20203)
  • Ensure later @source rules can re-include files excluded by earlier @source not rules (#20203)
  • Upgrade: don't migrate empty class rules to invalid @utility rules (#20205)
  • Ensure transitions between inset-shadow-none and other inset shadows work correctly (#20208)
  • Ensure explicitly referenced @source directories are scanned even when ignored by git (#20214)
  • Ensure @source globs ending in **/* preserve dynamic path segments to avoid scanning too many files (#20217)
  • Canonicalization: don't fold calc(…) divisions when the result would require high precision (e.g. w-[calc(100%/3.5)] → w-[calc(100%/3.5)], not w-[28.571428571428573%]) (#20221)
  • Serve ESM type declarations to ESM importers of @tailwindcss/postcss (#20228)

Changed

  • Generate 0 instead of calc(var(--spacing) * 0) for spacing utilities like m-0 and left-0 (#20196)

Fixed

  • Support bare spacing values for auto-rows-* and auto-cols-* utilities (e.g. auto-rows-12 and auto-cols-16) (#20229)

  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing in Deno v2.8.x when context.parentURL is not a valid URL (#20245)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode rebuilds when the input CSS file changes in an ignored directory (#20246)
  • Allow @variant rules used in addBase(...) to use custom variants defined later (#20247)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing during HMR when scanned files or directories are deleted (#20259)
  • Generate font-size instead of color declarations for text-[--spacing(...)] (#20260)
  • Prevent @source patterns from scanning unrelated sibling files and folders (#20263)
  • Extract class candidates adjacent to Template Toolkit delimiters like %]...[% in .tt, .tt2, and .tx files (#20269)
  • Extract class candidates from conditional Maud syntax like p.text-black[condition] (#20269)
  • Prevent @position-try rules from triggering unknown at-rule warnings when optimizing CSS (#20277)
  • Support class suggestions for named opacity modifiers from --opacity theme values (#20287)
  • Prevent type errors in @tailwindcss/postcss when used with newer PostCSS patch releases (#20289)

[4.3.1] - 2026-06-12

Added

  • Add --silent option to suppress output in @tailwindcss/cli (#20100)

Fixed

  • Remove deprecation warnings by using Module#registerHooks instead of Module#register on Node 26+ (#20028)
  • Canonicalization: don't crash when plugin utilities throw for unsupported values (#20052)
  • Allow @apply to be used with CSS mixins (#19427)
  • Ensure not-* correctly negates @container queries, including style(...) queries (#20059)
  • Ensure drop-shadow-* color utilities work with custom shadow values containing calc(...) (#20080)
  • Fix 'Sourcemap is likely to be incorrect' warnings when using @tailwindcss/vite (#20103)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/webpack can be installed in Rspack projects without requiring webpack as a peer dependency (#20027)
  • Canonicalization: don't suggest invalid calc(...) expressions (e.g. px-[calc(1rem+0px)] → px-[calc(1rem+0)]) (#20127)
  • Canonicalization: avoid suggesting large spacing-scale values for arbitrary lengths (e.g. left-[99999px] → left-[99999px], not left-24999.75) (#20130)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode recovers when a tracked dependency is deleted and restored (#20137)
  • Ensure standalone @tailwindcss/cli binaries are ignored when scanning for class candidates (#20139)
  • Ensure class candidates are extracted from Twig addClass(...) and removeClass(...) calls (#20198)
  • Don't crash in the Ruby or Vue preprocessors when scanning files containing invalid UTF-8 bytes (#19588)
  • Allow @variant to be used inside addBase (#19480)
  • Ensure @source globs with symlinks are preserved (#20203)
  • Ensure later @source rules can re-include files excluded by earlier @source not rules (#20203)
  • Upgrade: don't migrate empty class rules to invalid @utility rules (#20205)
  • Ensure transitions between inset-shadow-none and other inset shadows work correctly (#20208)
  • Ensure explicitly referenced @source directories are scanned even when ignored by git (#20214)
  • Ensure @source globs ending in **/* preserve dynamic path segments to avoid scanning too many files (#20217)
  • Canonicalization: don't fold calc(...) divisions when the result would require high precision (e.g. w-[calc(100%/3.5)] → w-[calc(100%/3.5)], not w-[28.571428571428573%]) (#20221)

items.old:
## What

`kci_engine` and `kmg_engine` in `src/database.py` each opened a plain
`create_engine(url, future=True)` — no `connect_args`, no WAL mode. Both
point at on-disk SQLite files that other independently-scheduled services
also read/write directly:

- `data/competitors.db` is **kinz-competitor-intelligence**'s own database
  (its scraper + dashboard write to it on their own schedule).
- `data/margin.db` is **kinz-margin-guardian-pipeline**'s own database.

This bridge is a third process touching both files from outside, on its
own APScheduler interval, with zero lock-contention handling — a write
from here landing mid-write from either of those other processes fails
instantly with `database is locked` instead of waiting.

## Fix

`kinz-competitor-intelligence`'s own `src/database.py` already solves
this exact problem for its one database: WAL journal mode + a 30s
`busy_timeout` applied via a per-connection `event.listens_for(engine,
"connect")` listener (`busy_timeout` doesn't persist to the file the way
`journal_mode` does — every pooled connection needs it applied). Ported
the same pattern here, to both engines.

Also had to `os.makedirs` the parent directory before the eager
`engine.connect()` that sets WAL on the file — `data/` is gitignored and
doesn't exist on a fresh checkout, so a naive port of the pattern broke
every test at collection with `unable to open database file` until this
was added. Caught by actually running the suite, not just reading the
diff — see verification below.

## Verification

- Before this directory fix: `pytest -q` failed all 38 tests at
  collection (`sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: unable to open database
  file`).
- After: `pytest -q` → 38 passed.
- `ruff check .` → all checks passed.

items.old:
## What

Adds a price-outlier guard in front of the sync write. Before `sync_latest_prices()` writes a `MarketPriceSnapshot`, it now compares the new price to the most recent snapshot already on file for the same product+competitor pair. If the new price is more than `PRICE_OUTLIER_MAX_RATIO` (default `5.0`) times higher, or less than `1/5.0` times lower, than that last snapshot, the write is skipped and a structured `sync_price_outlier_rejected` warning is logged instead.

**Why:** the whole point of this bridge is to feed trustworthy market prices into the margin-guardian pipeline. Right now a single scraper glitch upstream in `kinz-competitor-intelligence` (misread decimal, wrong currency parsed, stale/broken HTML) sails straight through into a `MarketPriceSnapshot` with no check at all, and margin-guardian would compute a margin comparison against a bogus number. This wasn't on the existing backlog (`docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`) — a gap the closed loop wouldn't have queued up on its own.

First-time syncs (no prior KMG snapshot to compare against) and ordinary price changes are unaffected — only pairs with an existing snapshot and an implausible jump are held back.

## Success criterion (written before implementing, verbatim)

## What was wrong

`Deduplicator` (`src/astk/alerts.py`) was in-memory and per-process only, so N Airflow workers, N Gunicorn workers, or a task retried on a different host each maintain independent suppression state — exactly the scenario alert dedup exists to prevent. This was tracked as item 5 in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`, ranked as "the first functional gap that plausibly blocks a real service from adopting the library rather than merely inconveniencing it."

## What changed

- `DedupBackend` is now a `Protocol` with one atomic method: `claim(key: str, ttl: timedelta) -> bool`.
- `InMemoryDedupBackend` is the previous per-process logic, extracted unchanged in behaviour.
- `PostgresDedupBackend(engine, table_name="astk_alert_dedup")` does a single atomic upsert, not read-then-write:
  ```sql
  INSERT INTO astk_alert_dedup (key, expires_at) VALUES (:key, :expires_at)
  ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET expires_at = :expires_at
      WHERE astk_alert_dedup.expires_at < now()
  RETURNING key
  ```
  A returned row means the claim was won — two workers racing on the same key against the same database produce exactly one `True`.
- `create_dedup_table(engine, table_name=...)` ships the idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, DDL also in the docstring for consumers who'd rather paste it into their own migrations.
- `Deduplicator(ttl_s=...)` is **unchanged** (back-compat) and now also accepts `backend=`.
- Table names are validated against a safe-identifier regex before being interpolated into SQL (identifiers can't be bind parameters).
- Registered the `postgres` pytest marker in `pyproject.toml` so it doesn't warn.

**Split from the backlog item, not bundled:** the original item 5 also asked for "wired into CI with a Postgres service container." That requires editing the *existing* `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which this loop's merge rules keep as a separate, owner-reviewed change (and this sandbox has no Postgres to verify such a workflow against before pushing it). Left as item 5b in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`.

## How it was verified

```
$ ruff check .
All checks passed!

$ pytest --cov=astk --cov-report=term-missing -q
..........................s................................s............ [ 94%]
....                                                                     [100%]
74 passed, 2 skipped in 3.04s
TOTAL   412  33  92%    (was 60 passed / 1 skipped / 91% before this PR)
```

`tests/test_dedup_backends.py` (+15 tests) covers `InMemoryDedupBackend` directly, `Deduplicator`'s delegation to an injected backend, and `PostgresDedupBackend`'s SQL-building path against a fake engine/connection (asserts the exact `ON CONFLICT`/`RETURNING`/`WHERE ... < now()` clauses and bind params, and that it's exactly one `execute()` call, not a select followed by a write).

**Proved the tests are load-bearing**, not tests that would pass against anything: reverted `src/astk/alerts.py` to the pre-change code and reran —

```
$ git stash push -- src/astk/alerts.py
$ pytest tests/test_dedup_backends.py tests/test_alerts.py -q
ImportError: cannot import name 'InMemoryDedupBackend' from 'astk.alerts'
1 error in 0.18s
$ git stash pop
$ pytest -q
74 passed, 2 skipped in 1.97s
```

## What was not covered

- **The real-Postgres concurrency path.** There is no Postgres instance in this environment. A `@pytest.mark.postgres` test (two threads racing `claim()` on the same key, asserting exactly one winner) is written and included, but it's skipped unless `ASTK_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set, and has never actually executed — here or anywhere, since CI doesn't have a Postgres service container wired up yet. That wiring is item 5b, intentionally left out of this PR (see "split from the backlog item" above).
- Docs updated to match: `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` (5a done, 5b spun out), `README.md` ("What's here" + "What's not built yet"), `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased).

## What changed

Backlog item 4 ("establish a version contract") bundled a code/docs half and
a publish action (tag `v0.1.0` + cut a GitHub release). Split it in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`
into 4a (this PR) and 4b (owner action — cutting a release on a public repo
is outside what this loop takes on its own authority). See the backlog file
for the split rationale.

This PR:
- Adds `CHANGELOG.md` in Keep a Changelog format (`Unreleased` + `0.1.0` entry
  covering the initial module set and the correctness fixes from items 2/3).
- Makes `astk.__version__` read from
  `importlib.metadata.version("analytics-service-toolkit")` — the pip
  distribution name, **not** the `astk` import name — instead of a hardcoded
  string literal, with a `PackageNotFoundError` fallback to the
  `pyproject.toml` value for the uninstalled/editable case.
- Adds a "Compatibility" section to `README.md` documenting the pre-1.0
  policy (minor bumps may break, patch bumps never do).
- Corrects two stale test-count figures in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` (the
  backlog's own "current state" line, and item 2's cross-reference) found
  while touching that file.

## Why

Four KINZ services depend on this library from an unpinned default branch.
A version contract is the precondition for pinning to be meaningful once the
owner cuts 4b.

## Verified

- `pytest --cov=astk --cov-report=term-missing`: 60 passed, 1 skipped, 91%
  coverage (was 57 passed / 1 skipped before this change).
- `ruff check .`: clean.
- **The new test actually catches the bug it's meant to catch.** A plain
  `astk.__version__ == pyproject_version` equality check can't distinguish
  "correctly read from installed package metadata" from "silently fell back
  to a hardcoded literal that happens to equal the same string" — both are
  currently `"0.1.0"`. So `tests/test_version.py` also monkeypatches
  `importlib.metadata.version` and reloads the module to pin the *exact*
  distribution name queried. Proved this catches a real mistake: I initially
  wrote `version("astk")` (the import name) instead of
  `version("analytics-service-toolkit")` (the pip distribution name) — the
  equality-only test passed anyway (coincidentally equal), the pinned-name
  test failed correctly. Reintroduced that exact bug against the final code
  and confirmed only the new test fails; restored the fix and confirmed the
  full suite (60/1) passes again.

## NOT covered

- 4b (tag `v0.1.0`, cut the GitHub release, pin the README install line) —
  left for the owner; see `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` item 4b.
- Item 1 (`kinz-price-bridge` adoption) remains blocked — it requires editing
  a different repo, out of scope here, already flagged in an earlier cycle.

items.old:
## What

`docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` already documented this as a real blocker:
`kinz-competitor-intelligence` sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` +
`busy_timeout=30000` on every pooled SQLite connection so its scraper can
write while the dashboard reads. `astk.db.make_engine` had no equivalent
handling for file-backed SQLite — only the `:memory:` case got any
special treatment — so that repo's own `database.py` duplicates this by
hand, and `kinz-price-bridge` now does too (separate PR, same underlying
gap). Per this repo's own convention ("do at least two services already
duplicate this?"), that's a clean extraction target, not a speculative
addition.

## Fix

`make_engine()` now attaches a `connect`-event listener that sets both
PRAGMAs on every connection it opens, for both file-backed and
`:memory:` SQLite URLs (WAL is a silent no-op on `:memory:` — SQLite
always uses "memory" journal mode there — so applying it unconditionally
is harmless). Also widens the sqlite `connect_args` to include
`timeout=30`, matching `kinz-competitor-intelligence`'s own
belt-and-suspenders approach — a connect-time timeout plus the
`busy_timeout` PRAGMA, since `busy_timeout` doesn't persist to the file
the way `journal_mode` does and must be reapplied per pooled connection.

Deliberately does **not** add an eager `engine.connect()` or create any
missing parent directory. `test_healthcheck_false_for_broken_engine`
already exercises `make_engine()` against an unreachable absolute path
and expects it to stay lazy and non-throwing, with the failure surfacing
via `healthcheck()` returning `False` rather than an exception here — I
almost broke that test by porting `kinz-price-bridge`'s own `mkdir` fix
(correct in that repo, where the missing directory is a real, private
`data/` path meant to exist) into this shared, cached constructor, where
it isn't appropriate. Added a regression test pinning that this stays
true.

## Verification

- `pytest --cov=astk --cov-report=term-missing` → 57 passed (was 52), 1
  skipped, `db.py` 95% coverage
- `ruff check .` → all checks passed

## What changed
Verified `docs/ADOPTION.md` (backlog item 3) against the actual source of all four KINZ consumer repos, via fresh read-only shallow clones — the original doc was written from README/file-layout alone and never checked. Rewrote every row with concrete `path/to/file.py:LINE` evidence or an explicit `UNVERIFIED`/corrected marker, and added a Blocker column per repo. Also updated `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`'s header, which claimed 'zero real consumers' — that's no longer true.

## Why
This doc is the pitch deck for the library. If its specifics are wrong, the first engineer to check loses trust in the whole repo, and it directly feeds the roadmap (items 5/6 ranking depends on real blockers, not guesswork).

## Key findings
- **`kinz-margin-guardian-pipeline` already imports `astk.settings`/`astk.db`/`astk.alerts` in production code.** This is a real consumer today. Its Dashboard concern is the one row still unadopted, and it's now an inconsistency bug: `dashboard/app.py` hand-rolls `create_engine()` instead of reusing the `astk.db.make_engine` its own `api/database.py` already imports two files over.
- **`kinz-competitor-intelligence`: a real, previously-undocumented blocker.** `astk.db.make_engine` has no WAL-mode/`busy_timeout` handling for file-backed SQLite; this repo sets both on every pooled connection so the scraper can write while the dashboard reads concurrently. Migrating its DB layer to `astk.db` as-is would silently drop that and reintroduce locking failures.
- **`kinz-secure-commerce-hub`: another undocumented blocker.** Its own settings class fails fast on known-insecure default secrets in production; `astk.settings.BaseServiceSettings` has no equivalent check — adopting it as-is would be a silent security regression. Also corrected: the 'nightly reconciliation job / alerting it grows' language described something that doesn't exist in the repo yet.
- **`kinz-accounting-analysis-*`'s DB row was already correctly absent** — no SQL database exists in that repo (file-based CSV/Parquet only). Confirmed, not assumed.

```
.venv/bin/ruff check .
All checks passed!

.venv/bin/pytest --cov=astk --cov-report=term-missing -q
54 passed, 1 skipped, 92% coverage (unchanged from main — docs-only change)
```

- No code changes — docs only.
- No line-count deletion estimates (the item's acceptance criteria asked for them, but most rows resolved to 'not adopted, real blocker' rather than a clean before/after diff to measure from — noted in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` as follow-up once a real diff exists).

## 1. Success criterion (verbatim, written before implementing)

> `astk` currently gives a consuming service no sanctioned way to read the real value of a
> `SecretStr` / `PostgresDsn` settings field, and its own `README.md` "Quick start" calls
> `str(settings.slack_webhook_url)` and `str(settings.database_url)` — which under pydantic v2
> yield the masked string `"**********"` for an unwrapped `SecretStr` (and the literal `"None"`

> Slack alert to the URL `"**********"`, where `SlackNotifier` swallows the resulting `httpx`
> error and returns `AlertResult(ok=False)` — the alert is silently lost with nothing raised.
>

>
> 1. `BaseServiceSettings` gains two documented accessor methods:
>    - one that returns the real Slack webhook URL as a plain `str` (e.g.
>      `"https://hooks.slack.com/services/T/B/XXXX"`, NOT `"**********"`) when `slack_webhook_url`
>      is set, and `None` when it is unset;
>    - one that returns the real database URL as a plain `str` when `database_url` is set, and
>      raises `SettingsError` whose message contains the substring `database_url` (or
>      `DATABASE_URL`) when it is unset — never returning the string `"None"`.
>
> 2. `SlackNotifier.__init__` rejects a webhook URL that does not start with `http://` or
>    `https://` by raising `ValueError` at construction time. In particular
>    `SlackNotifier("**********")` raises `ValueError`.
>
> 3. `README.md`'s "Quick start" no longer calls `str()` on `settings.slack_webhook_url` or
>    `settings.database_url`; it uses the new accessors.
>
> 4. New tests that:
>    - (behavioral regression proof) check out the base commit and confirm that on the OLD code
>      `SlackNotifier("**********").send(Alert(title="t", body="b"))` returns `AlertResult(ok=False)`
>      and raises nothing; and confirm that on the NEW code `SlackNotifier("**********")` raises
>      `ValueError` before any `.send()` call;
>    - confirm the new settings accessor returns `"https://hooks.slack.com/x"` (not `"**********"`)
>      for a set webhook, and that the db accessor raises `SettingsError` mentioning the field
>      name when the URL is unset;
>    - a valid `SlackNotifier("https://hooks.slack.com/x", client=<fake>)` still sends normally
>      (`ok=True`) — no regression to the existing happy path.

  (symbol-existence), which is the weaker kind of proof.

**Substantive defects the verifier found (beyond the test-design miss) — for the owner to weigh:**
1. **Secret leakage in the new error message.** `alerts.py` embeds `{webhook_url!r}` in the
   `ValueError`, and `astk doctor` prints it to stdout. In a repo whose `settings.py` exists to
   redact secrets, a user who typos a scheme on a real webhook (`hooks.slack.com/services/T/B/REALTOKEN`)
   gets the full token printed to console + any captured traceback.

   `astk alert t b --webhook-url '**********'` now dies with an uncaught traceback and no output
   (was: `ok=False attempts=3 …`). Exit code still 1, so no existing CLI test catches it. Also
   rubs against `CLAUDE.md`'s "Notifiers must never raise into the caller".
3. **Over-strict scheme check.** `SlackNotifier("HTTPS://hooks.slack.com/x")` (uppercase scheme,
   valid to `httpx`) is now rejected. Compliant with the criterion's literal wording, still a
   latent support ticket. No `.strip()` either, so a trailing newline from `.env` is rejected.

   `_env_file` override, so a developer with a local `.env` in the repo root (gitignored) makes
   them fail. Pre-existing tests avoid this by passing `env_file=str(tmp_path / ".env")`; the
   new tests break that convention. CI (clean checkout) is unaffected.

Backlog item 2 in `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` — "verify and fix `dashboard.cached_query()`".

## What changed

- **`src/astk/dashboard.py`** — replaced the per-call nested `@st.cache_data` closure in `cached_query` with a single module-level `_cached_fetch_df(_engine, url, sql, params)` decorated once. Public signature is now `cached_query(engine, sql, params=None)`.
- **`tests/test_dashboard.py`** — +4 tests.
- **`docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`** — item 2 marked done; item 1 flagged as blocked on the genesis loop (kinz-price-bridge); re-pointed the "next item" marker.

## Why

The suspected bug ("cache never hits across reruns, SQL re-runs every time") **is not real** — `st.cache_data` keys its namespace on the wrapped function's `__module__` + `__qualname__` + source hash, all stable across the re-created closure. `test_cached_query_reuses_the_cache_on_a_repeated_identical_call` confirms it and passes against the old code too.

The **real** bug: `engine` was captured in that closure, *outside* the cache key. So:

- `cached_query(engine_a, "SELECT 1")` then `cached_query(engine_b, "SELECT 1")` (different databases) → `engine_b` silently gets `engine_a`'s rows.
- No `params` argument at all → parameterised queries can't be cached per-parameter-set.

New key is `(str(engine.url), sql, tuple(sorted(params)))` — all hashable. `_engine` is passed under a leading-underscore name so Streamlit ignores it when hashing. `ttl` is now the module constant `CACHED_QUERY_TTL_S` (60s, unchanged default) — `st.cache_data` only accepts `ttl` at decoration time, which is *why* the old code recreated the wrapper per call.

## Breaking change

Third positional arg went from `ttl_s: int = 60` to `params: dict | None = None`. Acceptable: zero consumers (IMPROVEMENTS.md item 1), and `cached_query` was unused even by `examples/demo_app.py`. Should be folded into the `CHANGELOG.md` `0.1.0` entry when backlog item 4 lands.

## Verified

- `ruff check .` — clean
- `pytest --cov=astk` — 40 passed / 1 skipped (was 36/1), coverage 89% → 91%, `dashboard.py` 80% → 89%
- Regression proof: `git stash` the `dashboard.py` fix → `test_cached_query_does_not_serve_one_engines_rows_to_another` fails `assert 1 == 2`; `git stash pop` → green.

## Not covered

- No `AppTest`-level rerun test — the backlog allowed for it "if the unit-level harness is not convincing"; the monkeypatched-`fetch_df` counter under bare-mode caching reproduces rerun behaviour directly, so it wasn't needed.
- `examples/demo_app.py` still calls `fetch_df` directly rather than `cached_query`; wiring the demo to the cached path is left for backlog item 1's integration work.
- `sidebar_filters` (the other untested dashboard helper) is untouched.

## What

Adds `feed_quality_gate.report.to_html()` and a `fqg check --html PATH` flag: a single, dependency-free HTML page — a score gauge plus a colour-coded PASS/FAIL/WARN table per check, and a sample of quarantined row ids — for anyone who would rather open a file than pipe the JSON report through `jq` or read a terminal transcript.

This is this week's `cloud-creative` pick (one new idea per week, checked against a goal written before the code): [experiment file](https://github.com/nassim0014/loop-engine-state/blob/main/experiments/2026-09-26-feed-quality-gate-html-report.md), committed before any code.

## Why this shape

## What changed

Implements `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` item 1: `checks.per_source_completeness`.

A feed-wide missing-value rate hides a single source collapsing — 16% missing
overall can be one source missing 80% of its own rows, averaged against a
healthy 40-row source, and no existing check sees the source-level number.

- New `PerSourceCompletenessRule` (`feed_quality_gate/rules.py`), disabled by
  default since it names a `column` and `source_column` that don't exist until
  a rules file configures them (existing rules files keep working unchanged).
- New `checks.check_per_source_completeness` (`feed_quality_gate/checks.py`):
  groups by `source_column`, applies `max_null_ratio` to each source
  independently, and reports each offending source's own
  count/total/ratio in `details["offending_sources"]` plus a sample of its
  offending row ids — not just a boolean, per the backlog item's ask.
  `min_source_rows` skips cohorts too small for a missing rate to be
  meaningful.
- Wired into `gate.evaluate()` behind `rules.per_source_completeness.enabled`.
- Documented (commented, disabled) in `rules.example.yaml`; README's "not
  built yet" list and test count updated.
- `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`: item 1 moved to "Done" with a dated note.

## Why

Per `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`: *"a global missing-price rate of ~6% can hide one
source that is missing prices on 79% of its own catalogue... a single
collapsed source is invisible in [the global average], and that source's
products then silently vanish from every downstream comparison."*

## Tests

- `tests/test_checks.py::TestPerSourceCompleteness` (9 tests): the boundary
  case, `min_source_rows`, both missing-column paths, an empty feed, the
  id-column fallback, and a NaN source value.
- `tests/test_gate.py::TestPerSourceCompletenessInEvaluate` (2 tests): the
  headline case — a feed whose 16% feed-wide missing rate clears a 20% column
  tolerance but whose one collapsed source (80% missing) trips a 10%
  per-source one — plus confirming the check stays off when unconfigured.
- New `multi_source_feed` synthetic fixture in `tests/conftest.py` (invented
  data, per repo convention).

## How I checked it

```
pytest -q            # 56 passed (was 45)
ruff check .          # clean
fqg check -i examples/sample_feed.csv -r rules.example.yaml   # still exits 1, unaffected (rule disabled)
```

## What changed

Backlog **item 0** — the only item in the "Blocked" section, and the one the
backlog says to do "before item #1".

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (new) — the repo had **no CI**. This is the
  workflow the genesis run authored but could not push (its token lacked the
  `workflow` scope). Content is unchanged from
  `loop-engine/logs/2026-09-02-genesis-ci.yml`. It runs, per matrix leg
  (Python 3.11 and 3.12):
  1. `pip install -e ".[dev]"` — core + dev only; the `[astk]` extra is
     deliberately skipped (private repo, no CI credentials, and `astk` is an
     optional import by design).
  2. `ruff check .`
  3. `pytest -q`
  4. CLI smoke test: `fqg check` against the intentionally-broken
     `examples/sample_feed.csv` must **exit 1**. A 0 means the gate stopped
     detecting anything.
- **`README.md`** — replaced the "No CI yet" caveat with a description of what
  CI does; added a status badge.
- **`docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`** — moved item 0 from *Blocked* to *Done*; removed the
  now-empty *Blocked* section. This unblocks items #1–#5 (each adds a check, and
  CI on 3.11 + 3.12 is what stops the next check from regressing a prior one —
  the 3.11/3.12 split is where this repo's first dtype bug lived).

## Why

Adding data-quality checks (items #1–#5) without CI is how a regression slips in
unnoticed, especially across the pandas 2.x/3.x dtype boundary that already bit
this repo once. The workflow existed and was logic-verified; it just needed a
token with `workflow` scope to land.

## Verified (locally, before push)

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `pip install -e ".[dev]"` | clean |
| `ruff check .` | `All checks passed!` |
| `pytest -q` | **45 passed** |
| `fqg check -i examples/sample_feed.csv -r rules.example.yaml` | **exit 1** (gate correctly rejects the broken feed: freshness 41.7d > 7d, price completeness 25% > 2%) |

The workflow itself will be exercised for the first time by this PR's own CI run.

## NOT covered

- No check logic added — this is CI plumbing only. Items #1–#5 follow.
- Cannot self-merge: touches `.github/workflows/**`, so per the loop's
  merge-safety contract (rule 6) it must be reviewed by hand. Also the repo had
  no prior green CI baseline, so rule 5 blocks auto-merge regardless.
